Hence every F3 chromatid on the fixed strand is of the form

0^{p}1^{q}0^{r}1^{s}, p+q+r+s=5,

i.e. a binary word of length 5 with at most one 1→0 descent, a 0*1*0*1* word. The monotone, i.e. 1→0-free, words are N0=6. For a fixed descent at position k, 1≤k≤4, the prefix can be chosen in k ways ending in 1 and the suffix in 5−k ways beginning in 0, giving N_k=k(5−k) words with the unique descent at k. Summing

N1=∑_{k=1}^{4}k(5−k)=4+6+6+4=20

words with exactly one 1→0 descent. Hence on the fixed positive strand

N_F3 = N0+N1 =6+20=26

different haploid sequences can be produced by two successive one-crossover meioses. Six are the F1/F2 monotone 0*1* haplotypes 00000,00001,00011,00111,01111,11111, the other 20 are the genuine F3 0*1*0*1* recombinants, e.g. 00101,01001,01101,01011,… The six 2^5–26 words which contain two 1→0 descents, 01010,10101 and the four-shift family, are impossible with the fixed orientation.

Diploid counting from the 26 haploid types is 26²=676 ordered maternal/paternal pairs and 26·27/2=351 unordered diploid autosomes, the 6 monotone types accounting for the F2 pool.

Disagreement / conventions. The 26 count allows k=0,5 i.e. a crossover in the flanking telomeric intervals so that parental haplotypes can be recovered as gametes. With the strict internal-only convention 1≤k≤4 and 1≤a,b≤4 the F1 gamete pool is the four internal recombinants 0^{a}1^{5-a}, a=1..4, and the attainable F3 positive-strand chromatids are

01111,00111,00011,00001, 01011,01001,01101,00101,

i.e. 8 distinct haploid types, 8·9/2=36 unordered diploid genotypes, the 4 monotone F2 types plus 4 two-break types with a<k<b. Allowing telomeric cuts recovers the 15-word C(4+2,2) bound and the 26-word bound above; allowing the reciprocal orientation doubles the count to the familiar 30-word, ≤3-switch bound.

Current belief: with the usual telomeric-inclusive definition the positive-strand haploid diversity in F3 is the 26-word 0*1*0*1* set, 20 strictly novel recombinants on top of the 6 F2 monotone haplotypes. If diploid autosomes are required this is 351 unordered genotypes, 676 ordered. The internal-only, strictly recombinant version is the 8-haploid/36-diploid statement often quoted in textbooks.
reflection_text.3:
After round 0 the core combinatorial picture is stable across most colleagues.  
With the two founders written $P_{0}=0^{5},P_{1}=1^{5}$ on the arbitrarily chosen positive strand and the strand-asymmetry fixing the left→right order, an $F_{1}\to F_{2}$ gamete with one obligatory crossover at $k$ is $0^{k}1^{5-k}$, $0\le k\le5$.  With the $k=0,5$ telomeric limits included this is the $6$ monotone $0^{*}1^{*}$ haplotypes $s_{k}$.  An $F_{2}\to F_{3}$ gamete is the splice $R_{ijk}(t)=s_{i}(t)$ for $t\le k$, $s_{j}(t)$ for $t>k$, i.e. 
$0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d}$ with $a+b+c+d=5$, $a,b,c,d\ge0$.  The $1\to0$ descent can occur at most once, so the attainable positive-strand words are exactly the $a_{10}\le1$ words.

Counting them gives $N_{0}=6$ monotone words and for each descent position $k=1\ldots4$ $k(5-k)$ words with a unique $1\to0$ descent.  $\sum_{k}k(5-k)=20$.  Hence
$N_{F_{3}}^{\rm hap}=6+20=26$ distinct positive-strand haplotypes can be present in the $F_{3}$ gamete pool, $6$ of them the $F_{2}$ $0^{*}1^{*}$ set and $20$ genuinely new $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ recombinants.  In diploid form this is $26^{2}=676$ ordered and $\binom{26+1}{2}=351$ unordered autosomal genotypes.  Up to the fixed orientation this is the $6+\binom{6}{3}=26$ count quoted by Colleagues 1,4,5,6,7,8.  Allowing the reciprocal orientation restores the $BABA$ family and gives the familiar $30$ binary words with $\le3$ switches, $2\sum_{r}\binom4{r-1}$.

The counting is sensitive to the telomeric convention.  If a crossover is required to fall strictly between the five scored SNPs, $1\le k\le4$, the $F_{1}\to F_{2}$ pool is the four internal monotone haplotypes $0^{a}1^{5-a}$, $a=1\ldots4$.  With $a<k<b$ the only new $F_{3}$ mosaics are $0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b}$, four of them
$01011,01001,01101,00101$, giving $4+4=8$ distinct positive-strand chromatids, $8\times9/2=36$ unordered diploid autosomes, the textbook internal-only statement.  Formally allowing $k=0,5$ as telomeric loci gives the $C(n+g,g)=C(4+2,2)=15$ distinct $0\!-\!1$ mosaics, $5$ monotone $+10$ two-break, i.e. $11$ essentially different $0\to1$ haplotypes, $22$ with reciprocal counting, as noted by Colleague 3.  

Remaining uncertainty is the intended interpretation of “exactly one locus per generation”.  With telomeric crossovers counted as formal loci the $26$ haplotype / $351$ diploid genotype result is the operative $a_{10}\le1$ bound.  With strict internal crossovers only the $8$ haplotype / $36$ genotype bound is obtained, and the $15$ mosaic $C(4+2,2)$ bound is the customary $g=2$ breakpoint upper bound.  I am presently retaining the $26$ positive-strand haplotype, $20$ novel $F_{3}$ recombinants, $351$ unordered diploid autosomes result as the fixed-orientation count, noting the $8$-haplotype internal-only reduction.
reflection_text.1:
The two founders on the arbitrarily chosen + strand can be taken as
$A=0^{5},\,B=1^{5}$.  With the strand asymmetry a meiosis is the left-right
splice

$h_{1}\xrightarrow{k}h_{1}[1\!:\!k]\,h_{2}[k+1\!:\!5]$ ,

$k=0\ldots5$.  $F_{1}\!\to\!F_{2}$ therefore gives the monotone set

$S_{1}=\{s_{i}=0^{i}1^{5-i}:0\le i\le5\}$, $|S_{1}|=6$,

$0^{5},0^{4}1,0^{3}1^{2},0^{2}1^{3},0\,1^{4},1^{5}$ on the + strand.  An
$F_{2}$ individual carries $s_{i},s_{j}\in S_{1}$ and an $F_{2}\!\to\!F_{3}$
gamete is $s_{i}[1\!:\!k]\,s_{j}[k+1\!:\!5]$.
For $0<i<k<j$

$s_{i}[1\!:\!k]\,s_{j}[k+1\!:\!5]=0^{i}1^{\,k-i}0^{\,j-k}1^{\,5-j}
      =0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d}$,

$a=i,\;b=k-i>0,\;c=j-k>0,\;d=5-j$, $a+b+c+d=5$, i.e. a word with
at most one $1\to0$ descent, $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$.  If $i\ge k$ or
$j\le k$ the splice collapses to a monotone $0^{p}1^{5-p}$.

Hence with $k$ allowed to be $0\ldots5$ the attainable + strand words are
exactly the $0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d}$ with $a+b+c+d=5$.  The non-monotone
words are in bijection with increasing triples $0\le i<k<j\le5$,

$N_{nm}= \binom{6}{3}=20$,

and with the six monotone words

$N_{+}=6+20=26$,

$6$ $F_{2}$-type $0^{*}1^{*}$ haplotypes and $20$ $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$
$F_{3}$ haplotypes, e.g. $0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{j-k}1^{5-j}$.  The $20$ words are
the genuinely new $F_{3}$ chromosomes; the six monotone words are the
$F_{1}$/$F_{2}$ set.  In diploid notation this is $26^{2}=676$ ordered
and $\binom{26+1}{2}=351$ unordered $F_{3}$ autosomes.

The $N_{0}+N_{1}=6+20=26$ count is the $a_{10}\le1$ count
$N(n)=n+1+n(n-1)(n+1)/6$, $N(5)=26$, often quoted as $6+\binom{6}{3}$.
If the six completely parental strings are removed the novel $F_{3}$ set
is the $20$ $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ strings, the $20$ triples $i<k<j$.

Remark on the conventional internal-only convention.  If a crossover
is required to fall strictly between two scored SNPs, $k=1\ldots4$
and the $F_{1}$ pool is $s_{i},\,1\le i\le4$.  Then the attainable + strand
haplotypes are $0^{p}1^{5-p}$ with $1\le p\le4$ and the $i<k<j$ triples
with $1\le i<k<j\le4$, $\binom{4}{3}=4$ non-monotone words
$01011,01001,01101,00101$.  This gives $4+4=8$ distinct + strand
chromatids in $F_{3}$, $8\cdot9/2=36$ unordered diploid autosomes,
the usual $C(n+g,g)=C(4+2,2)=15$ $0\!-\!1$ mosaics with the two telomeric
parentals removed.  Up to reciprocal duplication the unrestricted
one-orientation bound is $26\to30$, the $30$ words with $\le3$ switches
usually quoted. ∎
reflection_text.4:
The five SNPs are $0\leftrightarrow1$ in the two founders
$P_{0}=0^{5}$ and $P_{1}=1^{5}$ on the arbitrarily chosen positive strand.
With the strand asymmetry a meiosis is the left-right splice

$h_{1}\xrightarrow{k}h_{1}[1:k]\,h_{2}[k+1:5]$

and a gamete is always taken left from the first homologue and right
from the second.  The $F_{1}\to F_{2}$ gamete pool is therefore

$S_{1}=\{0^{i}1^{5-i}\;:\;0\le i\le5\}$

the six monotone $0^{*}1^{*}$ words.  Let an $F_{2}$ plant carry
$h_{a}=0^{a}1^{5-a}$ and $h_{b}=0^{b}1^{5-b}$ and let the $F_{2}\to F_{3}$
cut be $k$.  Then on the positive strand

$R_{a b k}=h_{a}[1:k]h_{b}[k+1:5]=
0^{m}1^{k-m}0^{\,b-k}1^{5-b}$ ,
$m=\min(a,k)$, i.e. up to the $b\le k$ or $a\ge k$ trivialities

$R_{a b k}=0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{\,b-k}1^{5-b},\qquad 0\le a<k<b\le5 ,$

so that every $F_{3}$ chromatid is a $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ word

$0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d},\qquad a+b+c+d=5,\;a,b,c,d\ge0,$

with at most one $1\to0$ descent.  The monotone case $b=0$ or $c=0$
gives the six $F_{1}$ words $0^{i}1^{5-i}$, $0\le i\le5$.  The genuinely
new $F_{3}$ words are those with $b>0,c>0$,

$0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d},\;a\ge0,\;b\ge1,\;c\ge1,\;d\ge0,\;a+b+c+d=5$.

Put $b'=b-1,\;c'=c-1$.  Then $a+b'+c'+d=3$ and

$\#\{b>0,c>0\}= \binom{3+4-1}{3}= \binom{6}{3}=20$

distinct $0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d}$ words with a single $1\to0$ descent.
Together with the six monotone words

$\;|{\cal H}_{F_{3}}^{+}|=6+20=26\;$

different positive-strand chromatids can be present in the $F_{3}$
gamete pool, $6$ of them the $F_{1}/F_{2}$ monotone $0^{*}1^{*}$ haplotypes
$11111,01111,00111,00011,00001,00000$ and $20$ novel
$0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ haplotypes.  In particular there are $20$
strictly novel $F_{3}$ recombinants, e.g. $00101,01001,01101,\dots$,
the six words which are $1\to0\to1$ with two $1\to0$ descents,
$01010,10101,\dots$, being unattainable with two successive
one-crossover meioses in the fixed orientation.

The $26$ haplotypes give $26^{2}=676$ ordered maternal/paternal pairs
and $\binom{26+1}{2}=351$ unordered diploid autosomes in the $F_{3}$
intercross; discarding the two completely parental words the usual
text-book statement is the $24$ recombinant diploid types.

Remark on conventions.  If the crossover is required to lie strictly
inside the five-site interval, $1\le k\le4$ and $1\le a,b\le4$, the
$F_{1}\to F_{2}$ pool is the four internal monotone words
$0^{a}1^{5-a}$, $1\le a\le4$.  Then $a<k<b$, $a,b,k\in\{1,\dots,4\}$,
gives $4$ novel two-break words $01011,01001,01101,00101$ and with the
four monotone words $8$ distinct positive-strand chromatids,
$8\cdot9/2=36$ unordered diploid autosomes, the familiar internal-only
count.  Allowing telomeric cuts $k=0,5$ restores the full $26$
positive-strand haplotypes quoted above, i.e. the $6+\binom{6}{3}$
count.  The $26\to30$ increase to $30$ words is obtained if the
reciprocal $B A B A$ orientation is reinstated.  This is the $a_{10}\le1$
family normally quoted for $n=5$ and $g=2$ meioses.
reflection_text.7:
The five SNPs can be labelled A = 0 on the positive strand and B = 1. With the strand asymmetry fixed the operation that a meiosis can perform on two homologues $a,b$ is 
$R_k(a,b)=a[1:k]b[k+1:5]$, $0\le k\le5$, i.e. the left block is kept from the
first homologue and the right block from the second one.  The F1 $\to$ F2
gamete pool is therefore the monotone $0^{*}1^{*}$ set 
$S_{1}=\{0^{i}1^{5-i}:0\le i\le5\}$, six positive–strand haplotypes, the
four internal $1\le i\le4$ being the strictly recombinant F1 gametes.

Let $a=s_{i},b=s_{j}\in S_{1}$ be the two homologues of an F2 individual
and let the F2 $\to$ F3 meiosis cut at $k$.  On the fixed orientation

$R_{ijk}=0^{a'}1^{k-a'}0^{c}1^{5-k-c}$,
$a'=\min(i,k),\;c=\max(0,j-k)$,
so every F3 gamete is of the form
$0^{p_{1}}1^{p_{2}}0^{p_{3}}1^{p_{4}}$ with $p_{1}+p_{2}+p_{3}+p_{4}=5$,
$p_i\ge0$, i.e. a word with at most one $1\to0$ descent.  The monotone
$0^{*}1^{*}$ words are the six $F_{2}$ types $s_{i}$.  With a unique
$1\to0$ descent at $k$, $1\le k\le4$, the prefix $0^{p_{1}}1^{k-p_{1}}$ can be
chosen in $k$ ways and the suffix $0^{p_{3}}1^{p_{4}}$ in $5-k$ ways, i.e.
$N_{k}=k(5-k)$ words with the descent at $k$.  

$\sum_{k=1}^{4}k(5-k)=4+6+6+4=20$ words with exactly one $1\to0$
descent.  Together with the six monotone words

$N_{F3}=6+20=26$

different positive–strand chromatids are attainable in two obligatory
single-crossover meioses with the orientation fixed.  The six monotone
words are the $F_{2}$ haplotypes $0^{i}1^{5-i}$, $0\le i\le5$, the $20$
genuinely new $F_{3}$ haplotypes are the $0^{p}1^{q}0^{r}1^{s}$ with
$0\le p< p+q< p+q+r\le5$, $20=\binom{6}{3}$ in number.  Up to ordering
this is $26^{2}=676$ ordered and $\binom{26+1}{2}=351$ unordered diploid
autosomal genotypes, $6$ monotone + $20$ recombinant haplotypes on the
arbitrarily chosen strand.

With the conventional internal-only convention $1\le i,j,k\le4$ the
parental $0^{5},1^{5}$ and the telomeric $k=0,5$ products are removed.
Then $S_{1}^{int}=\{0^{i}1^{5-i}:1\le i\le4\}$, $a<k<b$ gives the
four non-monotone words $01011,01001,01101,00101$.  Hence the strictly
internal obligatory-crossover pool is
$4$ monotone $+4$ $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ $=8$ distinct positive-strand
haplotypes, $8\cdot9/2=36$ unordered diploid autosomes, the $4$ new
$F_{3}$ haplotypes usually quoted.  This is the $8\to 36$ internal-only
version of the $26\to351$ count above.

The $26$ count is the $a_{10}\le1$ $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ family
$N(n)=n+1+n(n-1)(n+1)/6$.  For $n=5$, $N=26$, $20$ novel recombinants.
If reciprocal products are counted as distinct the familiar
$2\sum_{k=0}^{2}\binom4k=22$ $0\to1$ haplotypes, $11$ up to orientation,
is obtained.  The $8$-haplotype and $11/22$-haplotype statements in the
discussion are the internal-only / unrestricted-orientation versions of
the same construction.

8.text:
On the arbitrarily chosen positive strand write the two inbred founders as
$P_{0}=0^{5}$ and $P_{1}=1^{5}$.  With the one way asymmetry a meiosis
is the operation

$R_{k}(X,Y)=X[1:k]Y[k+1:5]$ , $0\le k\le5$,

so that after the $F_{1}\to F_{2}$ meiosis

${\cal H}_{1}=\{s_{i}=0^{i}1^{5-i}\;:\;0\le i\le5\}$

is the six monotone $0^{*}1^{*}$ gametes.  Up to the fixed orientation
this is the whole $F_{2}$ gametic pool.

Let $s_{i}=0^{i}1^{5-i}$ and $s_{j}=0^{j}1^{5-j}$ be the two homologues
carried by an $F_{2}$ individual and let the $F_{2}\to F_{3}$ meiosis cut
at $k$.  On the positive strand

$g_{ijk}=s_{i}[1:k]\,s_{j}[k+1:5]
       =0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d},\qquad a+b+c+d=5,$

i.e. a word of length $5$ with at most one $1\to0$ descent.  Writing
$a_{10}$ for the number of $10$ factors, $a_{10}\le1$ is the $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$
form.  A monotone word is $N_{1}=n+1$; a word with a unique $1\to0$
descent at $p$, $1\le p\le n-1$, has $p$ choices for the $0^{*}1^{*}$
prefix ending in $1$ and $n-p$ choices for the $0^{*}1^{*}$ suffix
starting in $0$, i.e. $p(n-p)$ words.

For $n=5$

$$
N_{10}(5)=\sum_{p=1}^{4}p(5-p)=4+6+6+4=20,
\qquad N_{1}(5)=6,
$$

so that

$$
N(5)=N_{1}+N_{10}=6+20=26
$$

different positive–strand chromatids can be generated by two successive
one-crossover meioses.  The six monotone words

$11111,01111,00111,00011,00001,00000$

are the $F_{2}$ types $s_{i}$ and the $20$ words

$0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b},\qquad0\le a<k<b\le5$,

are the genuinely novel $F_{3}$ recombinants, e.g. $01011,01001,
01101,00101,\dots$, $20$ of them being new on top of the six $F_{2}$
types.  The $2^{5}-26=6$ words with two $1\to0$ descents,
$01010$ and its $s$-shifts, are unattainable with the fixed orientation
and two single-crossover meioses.

In diploid form the $26$ haplotypes give $26^{2}=676$ ordered maternal/
paternal pairs and

$\displaystyle\binom{26+1}{2}=351$

unordered diploid autosomes in the $F_{3}$.  If the two parental
monotone haplotypes are removed the $20$ $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ words
are the novel $F_{3}$ chromatids usually quoted; with the conventional
internal-only convention $1\le k\le4$ this is the eight strictly
recombinant positive-strand haplotypes

$01111,00111,00011,00001,01011,01001,01101,00101$

$8$ per chromatid, $8\cdot9/2=36$ unordered diploid autosomes, the
$C(n+g,g)=C(4+2,2)=15$ $0\!-\!1$ mosaics including the telomeric
formal loci being the familiar textbook bound. ∎

4.text:
With the two founders written on the arbitrarily chosen positive strand

$$P_{0}=0^{5},\qquad P_{1}=1^{5},$$

a meiosis with the one way left–right splice

$$h_{1}\xrightarrow{k}h_{1}[1:k]\,h_{2}[k+1:5],\qquad0\le k\le5, $$

is a monotone splice.  Hence the $F_{1}\to F_{2}$ gamete pool on the
positive strand is

$${\cal H}_{1}=\{s_{i}=0^{\,i}1^{\,5-i}\;:\;0\le i\le5\},
\qquad |{\cal H}_{1}|=6 ,$$

the six $0^{*}1^{*}$ words $11111,01111,00111,00011,00001,00000$.
Let $h_{a}=0^{a}1^{5-a}$ and $h_{b}=0^{b}1^{5-b}$ be the two $F_{2}$
homologues and let the $F_{2}\to F_{3}$ cut be $k$.  On the positive
strand

$$R_{abk}=h_{a}[1:k]h_{b}[k+1:5]
      =0^{m}1^{k-m}0^{\,b-k}1^{\,5-b},\qquad m=\min(a,k), $$

i.e. up to the trivial $b\le k$ or $a\ge k$ cases

$$R_{abk}=0^{a}1^{\,k-a}0^{\,b-k}1^{\,5-b},
\qquad0\le a<k<b\le5 ,$$

a word of the form

$$0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d},\qquad a+b+c+d=5,\;a,b,c,d\ge0, $$

with at most one $1\to0$ descent.  Putting $b'=b-1,\;c'=c-1$ the
non–monotone words are $a+b'+c'+d=3$.  Hence

$$N_{10}=\#\{b>0,c>0\}= \binom{3+4-1}{3}= \binom{6}{3}=20$$

different $0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d}$ words with a single $1\to0$ descent.
With the six monotone $0^{*}1^{*}$ words

$$\bigl|{\cal H}_{F_{3}}^{+}\bigr|=6+N_{10}=6+20=26$$

different positive-strand chromatids can be present in the $F_{3}$
gamete pool.  The six monotone words are the $F_{1}/F_{2}$ haplotypes
$0^{i}1^{5-i}$, $0\le i\le5$, and the $20$ words $0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d}$
with $b>0,c>0$, e.g. $00101,01001,01101,00101\ldots$, are the
genuinely new $F_{3}$ recombinants.  In particular there are $20$
strictly novel $F_{3}$ positive-strand haplotypes, $6$ of them being the
$F_{2}$ $0^{*}1^{*}$ haplotypes.

In diploid terms the $26$ haplotypes give $26^{2}=676$ ordered and
$\binom{26+1}{2}=351$ unordered $F_{3}$ diploid autosomes.  Discarding
the two completely parental haplotypes the usual $24$ recombinant
diploid types are quoted.  With the conventional internal-only
convention $1\le k\le4$ this reduces to the $8$ positive-strand
haplotypes $0^{a}1^{5-a},\,1\le a\le4$ together with the four
two-break words $01011,01001,01101,00101$, i.e. $8$ chromatids,
$36$ unordered diploid autosomes. ∎

6.text:
On the arbitrarily chosen positive strand write the two founders as
$0^{5}$ and $1^{5}$ and let a $F_{1}\to F_{2}$ gamete be

$H_{1}(i)=0^{i}1^{5-i}$ , $0\le i\le 5$,

the $6$ monotone $0^{*}1^{*}$ words.  With the asymmetry fixed the
$F_{2}\to F_{3}$ gamete obtained from the two $F_{2}$ homologues
$H_{1}(i),H_{1}(j)$ with a cut at $k$ is

$g_{ijk}=H_{1}(i)[1\!:\!k]\,H_{1}(j)[k+1\!:\!5] $

on the positive strand.  Hence on the fixed strand

$g_{ijk}=0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d},\qquad a+b+c+d=5,\;a,b,c,d\ge0$,

i.e. a $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ word.  It is $1\to0$ free iff $c=0$ and the
six monotone words $0^{i}1^{5-i}$ are the $F_{2}$ pool.  Let the unique
$1\to0$ descent, if it exists, be between $k$ and $k+1$, $1\le k\le4$.
The prefix $g_{ijk}[1\!:\!k]$ has to be monotone and end in $1$ and can
be chosen in $k$ ways, the suffix $g_{ijk}[k+1\!:\!5]$ has to be monotone
and start in $0$ and can be chosen in $5-k$ ways.  Hence

$N_{k}=k(5-k)$

words have their unique $1\to0$ descent at $k$ and

$N_{1}=\sum_{k=1}^{4}k(5-k)=4+6+6+4=20$

words have exactly one $1\to0$ descent.  With the six monotone
$0^{*}1^{*}$ words

$N_{0}=6$,

on the fixed positive strand

$N_{F_{3}}=N_{0}+N_{1}=6+20=26$

different $5$-mer haplotypes can be generated by two successive
one-crossover meioses.  The six are the $F_{2}$ $0^{*}1^{*}$ haplotypes

$11111,01111,00111,00011,00001,00000$,

the other $20$ are the genuine $F_{3}$ $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ words,
e.g. $00101,01001,01101,01011\ldots$, $20$ novel recombinants on top of
the six $F_{2}$ types.

In ordered maternal/paternal notation this is $26^{2}=676$ $F_{3}$
gametic pairs and

$\displaystyle \binom{26+1}{2}=351$

unordered diploid autosomal genotypes on the fixed strand, the $6$
monotone types being the $F_{2}$ pool.  The $20$ $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$
words are the $C(6,3)=20$ strictly new $F_{3}$ haplotypes; discarding
the $k=0,5$ telomeric cuts the internal strictly recombinant set is
$4$ monotone $F_{1}$ types $01111,00111,00011,00001$ plus the four
two-break types $01011,01001,01101,00101$, i.e. $8$ positive-strand
haplotypes, $8^{2}=64$ ordered and $8\cdot9/2=36$ unordered diploid
autosomes, the textbook internal-only statement.  This is the $26\to30$
$ABAB$ count, $20$ novel $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ recombinants, often
quoted as $6+\binom{6}{3}=26$ distinct positive-strand $F_{3}$
chromosomes.

3.text:
On the arbitrarily chosen positive strand write the two founders as

$P_{0}=0^{5},\qquad P_{1}=1^{5}$

and let a meiosis with the strand asymmetry be the prefix–suffix
operation

$g_{k}(a,b)=a[1:k]\,b[k+1:5],\qquad 0\le k\le5$.

With one obligatory crossover the $F_{1}\to F_{2}$ gamete pool is the
monotone $0^{*}1^{*}$ set

${\cal H}_{1}=\{ s_{k}=0^{k}1^{5-k}:0\le k\le5\}$,

$|{\cal H}_{1}|=6$, the six $F_{2}$ chromatids.  Let $s_{i}=0^{i}1^{5-i}$,
$s_{j}=0^{j}1^{5-j}\in{\cal H}_{1}$ be the two $F_{2}$ homologues and let
the $F_{2}\to F_{3}$ meiosis cut at $k$.  On the fixed positive strand

$R_{ijk}(t)=s_{i}(t),\;t\le k;\qquad R_{ijk}(t)=s_{j}(t),\;t>k$,

i.e. with $a=\min(i,k)$, $b=k-a$, $c=\max(0,j-k)$

$R_{ijk}=0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{5-k-c}=0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d}$,
$a+b+c+d=5$,

so every $F_{3}$ chromatid is a $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ word.  In
particular a word can be written as a splice of two monotone blocks
iff it contains at most one $1\to0$ descent.  The monotone,
$1\to0$–free, words are

$N_{0}=n+1=6$, $0^{i}1^{5-i}$.

Let the unique $1\to0$ descent, if it exists, be at $p$, $1\le p\le4$.
The prefix $R[1:p]$ is monotone and ends in $1$ in $p$ ways and the
suffix $R[p+1:5]$ is monotone and starts in $0$ in $5-p$ ways, so

$N_{p}=p\,(5-p)$

words have the descent at $p$.  Hence

$N_{10}= \sum_{p=1}^{4}p(5-p)=4+6+6+4=20$

words with exactly one $1\to0$ descent, i.e. the genuine
$0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d}$ recombinants.  Up to the fixed orientation

$N_{F_{3}}^{\rm hap}=N_{0}+N_{10}=6+20=26$

different positive–strand chromatids can be present in the $F_{3}$
gamete pool, the six $s_{k}$ being the $F_{2}$ set and

$20=\displaystyle\binom{6}{3}$

of them being $0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d}$ with $0\le a<b<c\le5$ and
novel in $F_{3}$.  E.g. the $20$ new words are the $0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}
1^{5-b}$ with $0\le a<k<b\le5$.

In diploid form the $26$ haplotypes give $26^{2}=676$ ordered
maternal/paternal pairs and

$\displaystyle\binom{26+1}{2}=351$

unordered diploid autosomal genotypes in the $F_{3}$ intercross, $6$
of the haplotypes being the parental/ $F_{2}$ monotone set.

Remark on telomeric convention.  With a crossover required to fall
strictly between two scored SNPs, $1\le k\le4$ and $1\le a,b\le4$, the
$F_{1}\to F_{2}$ pool is the four internal monotone haplotypes
$0^{a}1^{5-a},a=1\ldots4$ and the $F_{2}\to F_{3}$ pool is confined to
the $0^{*}1^{*}$ words which start with $0$ and end with $1$.  There
are then $4$ $F_{2}$ haplotypes and the four two–break words
$01011,01001,01101,00101$, i.e. $8$ distinct positive–strand
chromatids, $8\times9/2=36$ unordered diploid autosomes, the usual
internal–only $C(n+g,g)=C(4+2,2)=15$ mosaic upper bound being
$5$ monotone $+$ $10$ two–break positive-strand haplotypes.  The
$26$–haplotype, $351$–genotype count above is the $k=0,5$ telomeric
convention normally quoted. ∎

5.text:
With the two founders written on the arbitrarily chosen strand as

* $P_{0}=0^{5},\qquad P_{1}=1^{5}$

and the orientation fixed so that a meiosis is the left–right splice

$g_{i,j,k}=h_{i}[1:k]\,h_{j}[k+1:5]$,

the $F_{1}\to F_{2}$ gametes are the monotone $0^{*}1^{*}$ words

${\cal H}_{1}=\{ s_{k}=0^{k}1^{5-k}:0\le k\le 5\}$ ,

$|{\cal H}_{1}|=6$, $s_{0}=11111$, $s_{5}=00000$ the two founders.
Let $s_{i},s_{j}\in{\cal H}_{1}$ be the two homologues carried by an
$F_{2}$ plant and let the $F_{2}\to F_{3}$ cross–over be at $k$.
On the fixed strand

$R_{ijk}=s_{i}[1:k]\,s_{j}[k+1:5]
      =0^{a}1^{\,k-a}0^{\,c}1^{\,5-k-c}$,
$a=\min(i,k),\;c=\max(0,j-k)$,

i.e. up to the fixed orientation an $F_{3}$ chromatid is a binary word of
length $5$ of the form

$0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d}, \qquad a+b+c+d=5,\;a,b,c,d\ge0,$

so that $a_{10}\le1$, at most one $1\to0$ descent.  The $1\to0$ free
words are the $6$ monotone $0^{i}1^{5-i}$.  For a unique descent at
$k$, $1\le k\le4$, the left $k$ block can be chosen in $k$ ways and the
right $5-k$ block in $5-k$ ways.  Hence

$N_{k}=k\,(5-k)$

words with the descent at $k$ and

$N_{10}=\sum_{k=1}^{4}k(5-k)=4+6+6+4=20$

words with exactly one $1\to0$ descent.  Together with the six monotone
words

$N_{F3}=N_{1}+N_{10}=6+20=26$

different positive-strand haplotypes can be made by two successive
obligatory single cross-overs in the fixed orientation.  The six
$0^{*}1^{*}$ words

$11111,01111,00111,00011,00001,00000$

are the $F_{2}$ pool and the $20$ words

$0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{\,b-k}1^{5-b},\qquad 0\le a<k<b\le5 $

i.e. $10111,10011,10001,10000,11011,11001,11000,01011,01001,01000,
11101,11100,01101,01100,00101,00100,11110,01110,00110,00010$,
are the genuinely new $F_{3}$ recombinants.  In particular the six
$2^{5}-26$ words containing two $1\to0$ descents, $01010,10101$ etc.,
are never made with the strand asymmetry fixed.

Hence there are $26$ distinct positive-strand chromatid sequences in
$F_{3}$, $6$ of them $F_{2}$-type and $20$ novel $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$
sequences.  In ordered diploid notation this is $26^{2}=676$ ordered
maternal/paternal pairs and $\binom{26+1}{2}=351$ unordered diploid
autosomes.  If the two telomeric cuts $k=0,5$ are discarded as
non-recombinant the internal-only pool is the $4$ internal $F_{2}$
haplotypes $0^{a}1^{5-a},1\le a\le4$ and the four two-break $F_{3}$
haplotypes $01011,01001,01101,00101$, i.e. $8$ positive-strand
haplotypes, $36$ unordered diploid autosomes, the usual $C(4+2,2)=15$
positive-strand bound being recovered when the parental $0^{5},1^{5}$
words are reinstated.  This is the $6+\binom{6}{3}=26$ $a_{10}\le1$
count, $20$ novel $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ haplotypes up to the six
$F_{2}$ monotone words. ∎

7.text:
On the arbitrarily chosen strand write the two founders as
$A=0^{5}$ and $B=1^{5}$ and, with the strand asymmetry fixed, put

$$R_{k}(X,Y)=X[1:k]Y[k+1:5],\qquad 0\le k\le5 ,$$

for the gamete which is transmitted on the positive strand.
The $F_{1}\to F_{2}$ gamete pool is therefore

$$S_{1}=\{s_{i}=0^{i}1^{5-i}:0\le i\le5\},$$
$|S_{1}|=6$, the six monotone $0^{*}1^{*}$ words.  The two parental
words are $s_{0}=1^{5}$ and $s_{5}=0^{5}$.

Let $a=s_{i},\,b=s_{j}\in S_{1}$ be the two homologues of an $F_{2}$
individual and let the $F_{2}\to F_{3}$ meiosis cut at $k$.  On the
fixed orientation

$$R_{k}(a,b)=a[1:k]b[k+1:5]
          =0^{a'}1^{k-a'}0^{c}1^{5-k-c},$$
$$a'=\min(i,k),\qquad c=\max(0,j-k),$$
i.e. every $F_{3}$ chromatid is a $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ word

$$0^{p_{1}}1^{p_{2}}0^{p_{3}}1^{p_{4}},\qquad p_{1}+p_{2}+p_{3}+p_{4}=5,
\;p_{i}\ge0,$$

with at most one $1\to0$ descent $a_{10}\le1$.  The monotone words are
the six $s_{i}$.  Let the unique $1\to0$ descent, if it exists, be at
$p$, $1\le p\le4$.  The $p$-prefix can be chosen in $p$ ways as a
monotone word ending in $1$ and the $5-p$ suffix in $5-p$ ways as a
monotone word beginning in $0$.  Hence

$$N_{p}=p\,(5-p)$$

words with the descent at $p$ and

$$N_{10}=\sum_{p=1}^{4}p(5-p)=4+6+6+4=20$$

$0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ words with exactly one $1\to0$ descent.
With the six monotone $0^{*}1^{*}$ words

$$N_{F3}=6+N_{10}=6+20=26$$

different positive-strand chromatids can be made by two obligatory
single-crossover meioses in the fixed orientation.  The six monotone
words are the $F_{2}$ haplotypes $s_{i}$ and the $20$ words

$$0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b},\qquad0\le a<k<b\le5, $$

are the genuinely new $F_{3}$ recombinants, $20=\binom{6}{3}$.  In
particular there are $6$ $F_{2}$-type haplotypes and $20$ novel
$F_{3}$ haplotypes on the arbitrarily chosen strand.

In diploid terms the $26$ haplotypes give
$26^{2}=676$ ordered maternal/paternal pairs and

$$\binom{26+1}{2}=351$$

unordered diploid autosomal genotypes in the $F_{3}$ intercross, the
$6$ monotone haplotypes corresponding to the $F_{2}$ gametes.

Remark.  With the usual internal-only convention $1\le k\le4$ the two
parental telomeric products $k=0,5$ are removed.  The $F_{1}\to F_{2}$
pool is then the four internal recombinants $0^{i}1^{5-i}$, $1\le i\le4$,
and the $F_{2}\to F_{3}$ pool on the fixed strand is

$$01111,00111,00011,00001,01011,01001,01101,00101,$$

$4$ monotone + $4$ $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ $=8$ distinct positive-strand
haplotypes, i.e. $8^{2}=64$ ordered and $\binom{8+1}{2}=36$ unordered
diploid autosomes, the $4$ new $F_{3}$ haplotypes $01011,01001,01101,
00101$ usually quoted.  This is the $8\to36$ internal-only version of
the $26\to351$ count above. ∎

1.text:
On the $+$ strand write the two inbred founders as

$$P_{0}=0^{5},\qquad P_{1}=1^{5}$$

and put for a crossover after $k$ markers

$$R_{k}(X,Y)=X[1:k]\,Y[k+1:5],\qquad 0\le k\le5 .$$

In the fixed left$\,\to\,$right orientation a $P_{0}/P_{1}$ meiosis can
only give the monotone $0\to1$ words

$$S_{1}=\{s_{i}=0^{i}1^{5-i}\;:\;0\le i\le5\},\qquad |S_{1}|=6,  $$

$11111,01111,00111,00011,00001,00000$, the $F_{1}\to F_{2}$ gamete pool.
Let $s_{i},s_{j}\in S_{1}$ be the two $F_{2}$ homologues.  With the
same fixed orientation the $F_{2}\to F_{3}$ gamete is

$$g_{ij k}=s_{i}[1:k]\,s_{j}[k+1:5] .$$

Writing $i<k<j$ the non-trivial splice is

$$g_{ijk}=0^{i}1^{\,k-i}0^{\,j-k}1^{\,5-j}
       =0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d},\qquad a+b+c+d=5,$$

i.e. a word with at most one $1\to0$ descent, a $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$
word.  For $i\ge k$ or $j\le k$ the splice collapses to a monotone
$s_{p}=0^{p}1^{5-p}$.  Hence on the chosen $+$ strand a $F_{3}$ chromatin
is a word

$$0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d},\qquad a+b+c+d=5,\;a,b,c,d\ge0,  $$

and $a_{10}\le1$.  The monotone $a_{10}=0$ class is

$$N_{1}=5+1=6,\qquad s_{i}=0^{i}1^{5-i}, $$

the $F_{2}$ haplotypes.  A word with exactly one $1\to0$ descent is
fixed by the position $p$ of the descent, $1\le p\le4$, the $p$-prefix
being a monotone word ending in $1$ and the $5-p$ suffix being a
monotone word starting in $0$.  The number of words with the descent
at $p$ is $p(5-p)$ and

$$N_{10}=\sum_{p=1}^{4}p(5-p)=4+6+6+4=20 .$$

Hence

$$N_{+}=N_{1}+N_{10}=6+\binom{6}{3}=6+20=26$$

different $+$ strand chromatids can be present in the $F_{3}$ gamete
pool.  Six of them are the $F_{2}$ monotone haplotypes
$0^{i}1^{5-i}$, $0\le i\le5$, and

$$N_{{\rm new}}=\binom{6}{3}=20$$

of them are genuinely new $F_{3}$ $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ haplotypes,
$0\le a<k<j\le5$, e.g. $0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{j-k}1^{5-j}$.  The $20$ triples
$a<k<j$ are the $20$ novel recombinant $+$ strand sequences; with the
six $F_{2}$ monotone types in the background there are $26$ distinct
single-chromosome $+$ strand sequences in $F_{3}$.

In diploid terms the $26$ haplotypes give $26^{2}=676$ ordered
maternal/paternal pairs and

$$\binom{26+1}{2}=351$$

unordered diploid autosomal genotypes in $F_{3}$.  Up to the
conventional internal-only convention $k=1\ldots4$ the $F_{1}\to F_{2}$
pool is the four internal recombinants $0^{a}1^{5-a}$, $1\le a\le4$, and
the $F_{2}\to F_{3}$ $+$ strand pool is the $4$ monotone $F_{2}$ types
together with the $4$ two-break types $01011,01001,01101,00101$, i.e.
$8$ distinct $+$ strand chromatids, $8^{2}=64$ ordered and
$8\cdot9/2=36$ unordered diploid autosomes, the usual $C(4+2,2)=15$
$0\!-\!1$ mosaic count with the two parental telomeric haplotypes
removed.  This is the $6+\binom63$ $a_{10}\le1$ count usually quoted as
the $F_{3}$ diversity with the fixed orientation. ∎

2.text:
On the strand which is followed by the asymmetric exchange a one–crossover
meiosis is the prefix–suffix splice

$$R_{k}(a,b)=a[1\!:\!k]\,b[k+1\!:\!5] ,\qquad 0\le k\le 5 ,$$

and with the two founders $P_{0}=0^{5}$ and $P_{1}=1^{5}$,

$$H_{1}(i)=0^{i}1^{\,5-i},\qquad 0\le i\le 5 ,$$

is the whole $F_{1}\!\to\!F_{2}$ gamete pool.  Put $a=H_{1}(i)$,
$b=H_{1}(j)$ in an $F_{2}$ heterozygote and let the second $F_{2}\!\to\!F_{3}$
meiosis cut at $k$.  On the positive strand

\begin{equation*}
R_{ijk}=H_{1}(i)[1\!:\!k]\,H_{1}(j)[k+1\!:\!5]
      =0^{\min(i,k)}1^{\,k-\min(i,k)}
        0^{\max(0,j-k)}1^{\,5-k-\max(0,j-k)} ,
\end{equation*}
i.e. up to the fixed orientation every $F_{3}$ chromatid is a
$0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ word

$$w=0^{p_{1}}1^{p_{2}}0^{p_{3}}1^{p_{4}},\qquad p_{1}+p_{2}+p_{3}+p_{4}=5,
\;p_{i}\ge0,$$

with at most one $1\to0$ descent.  The $1\to0$–free words are the
$5+1$ monotone words

$$N_{1}=6,\qquad 0^{i}1^{\,5-i}\;, $$

which are the whole $F_{2}$ pool $00000,00001,00011,00111,01111,11111$.
Let the unique $1\to0$ descent be at $k$, $1\le k\le4$.  The $k$-prefix
must be monotone and end in $1$ and the $5-k$ suffix must be monotone
and begin in $0$, so that for the fixed $k$

$$N_{k}=k\,(5-k)$$

different words have their unique descent at $k$.  Hence

$$N_{10}= \sum_{k=1}^{4}k(5-k)=4+6+6+4=20$$

words with exactly one $1\to0$ descent, e.g.

$$00101,01101,01001,01011,00110,01110,\dots$$

so that on the arbitrarily chosen positive strand

$$N_{F_{3}}=N_{1}+N_{10}=6+20=26$$

different single-chromosome haplotypes can be present in the $F_{3}$
gamete pool, $6$ of them being the $F_{1}$–type monotone
$0^{*}1^{*}$ haplotypes and $20$ of them being the genuine
$0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ $F_{3}$ recombinants.  In particular there are
$20$ strictly novel positive-strand haplotypes created in the
$F_{2}\to F_{3}$ meiosis, the six monotone $0^{i}1^{5-i}$ being already
present in $F_{2}$.

In diploid notation the $26$ haplotypes give $26^{2}=676$ ordered
maternal/paternal genotypes and

$$\binom{26+1}{2}=351$$

unordered diploid autosomal genotypes in the $F_{3}$.  The $20$
$0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ words are the $ \binom{6}{3}=20$ new
positive-strand mosaics usually quoted as the $F_{3}$ contribution; with
the conventional internal–only $1\le k\le4$ convention the internal
positive-strand pool is the four $F_{2}$ haplotypes $0^{a}1^{5-a}$,
$1\le a\le4$, together with the four two-break haplotypes
$01011,01001,01101,00101$, i.e. eight distinct positive-strand
chromatids, $36$ unordered diploids. ∎

public_text.8:
On the arbitrarily chosen positive strand write the two inbred founders as
$P_{0}=0^{5}$ and $P_{1}=1^{5}$.  With the one way asymmetry a meiosis
is the operation

$R_{k}(X,Y)=X[1:k]Y[k+1:5]$ , $0\le k\le5$,

so that after the $F_{1}\to F_{2}$ meiosis

${\cal H}_{1}=\{s_{i}=0^{i}1^{5-i}\;:\;0\le i\le5\}$

is the six monotone $0^{*}1^{*}$ gametes.  Up to the fixed orientation
this is the whole $F_{2}$ gametic pool.

Let $s_{i}=0^{i}1^{5-i}$ and $s_{j}=0^{j}1^{5-j}$ be the two homologues
carried by an $F_{2}$ individual and let the $F_{2}\to F_{3}$ meiosis cut
at $k$.  On the positive strand

$g_{ijk}=s_{i}[1:k]\,s_{j}[k+1:5]
       =0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d},\qquad a+b+c+d=5,$

i.e. a word of length $5$ with at most one $1\to0$ descent.  Writing
$a_{10}$ for the number of $10$ factors, $a_{10}\le1$ is the $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$
form.  A monotone word is $N_{1}=n+1$; a word with a unique $1\to0$
descent at $p$, $1\le p\le n-1$, has $p$ choices for the $0^{*}1^{*}$
prefix ending in $1$ and $n-p$ choices for the $0^{*}1^{*}$ suffix
starting in $0$, i.e. $p(n-p)$ words.

For $n=5$

$$
N_{10}(5)=\sum_{p=1}^{4}p(5-p)=4+6+6+4=20,
\qquad N_{1}(5)=6,
$$

so that

$$
N(5)=N_{1}+N_{10}=6+20=26
$$

different positive–strand chromatids can be generated by two successive
one-crossover meioses.  The six monotone words

$11111,01111,00111,00011,00001,00000$

are the $F_{2}$ types $s_{i}$ and the $20$ words

$0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b},\qquad0\le a<k<b\le5$,

are the genuinely novel $F_{3}$ recombinants, e.g. $01011,01001,
01101,00101,\dots$, $20$ of them being new on top of the six $F_{2}$
types.  The $2^{5}-26=6$ words with two $1\to0$ descents,
$01010$ and its $s$-shifts, are unattainable with the fixed orientation
and two single-crossover meioses.

In diploid form the $26$ haplotypes give $26^{2}=676$ ordered maternal/
paternal pairs and

$\displaystyle\binom{26+1}{2}=351$

unordered diploid autosomes in the $F_{3}$.  If the two parental
monotone haplotypes are removed the $20$ $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ words
are the novel $F_{3}$ chromatids usually quoted; with the conventional
internal-only convention $1\le k\le4$ this is the eight strictly
recombinant positive-strand haplotypes

$01111,00111,00011,00001,01011,01001,01101,00101$

$8$ per chromatid, $8\cdot9/2=36$ unordered diploid autosomes, the
$C(n+g,g)=C(4+2,2)=15$ $0\!-\!1$ mosaics including the telomeric
formal loci being the familiar textbook bound. ∎
public_text.4:
With the two founders written on the arbitrarily chosen positive strand

$$P_{0}=0^{5},\qquad P_{1}=1^{5},$$

a meiosis with the one way left–right splice

$$h_{1}\xrightarrow{k}h_{1}[1:k]\,h_{2}[k+1:5],\qquad0\le k\le5, $$

is a monotone splice.  Hence the $F_{1}\to F_{2}$ gamete pool on the
positive strand is

$${\cal H}_{1}=\{s_{i}=0^{\,i}1^{\,5-i}\;:\;0\le i\le5\},
\qquad |{\cal H}_{1}|=6 ,$$

the six $0^{*}1^{*}$ words $11111,01111,00111,00011,00001,00000$.
Let $h_{a}=0^{a}1^{5-a}$ and $h_{b}=0^{b}1^{5-b}$ be the two $F_{2}$
homologues and let the $F_{2}\to F_{3}$ cut be $k$.  On the positive
strand

$$R_{abk}=h_{a}[1:k]h_{b}[k+1:5]
      =0^{m}1^{k-m}0^{\,b-k}1^{\,5-b},\qquad m=\min(a,k), $$

i.e. up to the trivial $b\le k$ or $a\ge k$ cases

$$R_{abk}=0^{a}1^{\,k-a}0^{\,b-k}1^{\,5-b},
\qquad0\le a<k<b\le5 ,$$

a word of the form

$$0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d},\qquad a+b+c+d=5,\;a,b,c,d\ge0, $$

with at most one $1\to0$ descent.  Putting $b'=b-1,\;c'=c-1$ the
non–monotone words are $a+b'+c'+d=3$.  Hence

$$N_{10}=\#\{b>0,c>0\}= \binom{3+4-1}{3}= \binom{6}{3}=20$$

different $0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d}$ words with a single $1\to0$ descent.
With the six monotone $0^{*}1^{*}$ words

$$\bigl|{\cal H}_{F_{3}}^{+}\bigr|=6+N_{10}=6+20=26$$

different positive-strand chromatids can be present in the $F_{3}$
gamete pool.  The six monotone words are the $F_{1}/F_{2}$ haplotypes
$0^{i}1^{5-i}$, $0\le i\le5$, and the $20$ words $0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d}$
with $b>0,c>0$, e.g. $00101,01001,01101,00101\ldots$, are the
genuinely new $F_{3}$ recombinants.  In particular there are $20$
strictly novel $F_{3}$ positive-strand haplotypes, $6$ of them being the
$F_{2}$ $0^{*}1^{*}$ haplotypes.

In diploid terms the $26$ haplotypes give $26^{2}=676$ ordered and
$\binom{26+1}{2}=351$ unordered $F_{3}$ diploid autosomes.  Discarding
the two completely parental haplotypes the usual $24$ recombinant
diploid types are quoted.  With the conventional internal-only
convention $1\le k\le4$ this reduces to the $8$ positive-strand
haplotypes $0^{a}1^{5-a},\,1\le a\le4$ together with the four
two-break words $01011,01001,01101,00101$, i.e. $8$ chromatids,
$36$ unordered diploid autosomes. ∎
public_text.6:
On the arbitrarily chosen positive strand write the two founders as
$0^{5}$ and $1^{5}$ and let a $F_{1}\to F_{2}$ gamete be

$H_{1}(i)=0^{i}1^{5-i}$ , $0\le i\le 5$,

the $6$ monotone $0^{*}1^{*}$ words.  With the asymmetry fixed the
$F_{2}\to F_{3}$ gamete obtained from the two $F_{2}$ homologues
$H_{1}(i),H_{1}(j)$ with a cut at $k$ is

$g_{ijk}=H_{1}(i)[1\!:\!k]\,H_{1}(j)[k+1\!:\!5] $

on the positive strand.  Hence on the fixed strand

$g_{ijk}=0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d},\qquad a+b+c+d=5,\;a,b,c,d\ge0$,

i.e. a $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ word.  It is $1\to0$ free iff $c=0$ and the
six monotone words $0^{i}1^{5-i}$ are the $F_{2}$ pool.  Let the unique
$1\to0$ descent, if it exists, be between $k$ and $k+1$, $1\le k\le4$.
The prefix $g_{ijk}[1\!:\!k]$ has to be monotone and end in $1$ and can
be chosen in $k$ ways, the suffix $g_{ijk}[k+1\!:\!5]$ has to be monotone
and start in $0$ and can be chosen in $5-k$ ways.  Hence

$N_{k}=k(5-k)$

words have their unique $1\to0$ descent at $k$ and

$N_{1}=\sum_{k=1}^{4}k(5-k)=4+6+6+4=20$

words have exactly one $1\to0$ descent.  With the six monotone
$0^{*}1^{*}$ words

$N_{0}=6$,

on the fixed positive strand

$N_{F_{3}}=N_{0}+N_{1}=6+20=26$

different $5$-mer haplotypes can be generated by two successive
one-crossover meioses.  The six are the $F_{2}$ $0^{*}1^{*}$ haplotypes

$11111,01111,00111,00011,00001,00000$,

the other $20$ are the genuine $F_{3}$ $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ words,
e.g. $00101,01001,01101,01011\ldots$, $20$ novel recombinants on top of
the six $F_{2}$ types.

In ordered maternal/paternal notation this is $26^{2}=676$ $F_{3}$
gametic pairs and

$\displaystyle \binom{26+1}{2}=351$

unordered diploid autosomal genotypes on the fixed strand, the $6$
monotone types being the $F_{2}$ pool.  The $20$ $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$
words are the $C(6,3)=20$ strictly new $F_{3}$ haplotypes; discarding
the $k=0,5$ telomeric cuts the internal strictly recombinant set is
$4$ monotone $F_{1}$ types $01111,00111,00011,00001$ plus the four
two-break types $01011,01001,01101,00101$, i.e. $8$ positive-strand
haplotypes, $8^{2}=64$ ordered and $8\cdot9/2=36$ unordered diploid
autosomes, the textbook internal-only statement.  This is the $26\to30$
$ABAB$ count, $20$ novel $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ recombinants, often
quoted as $6+\binom{6}{3}=26$ distinct positive-strand $F_{3}$
chromosomes.
public_text.3:
On the arbitrarily chosen positive strand write the two founders as

$P_{0}=0^{5},\qquad P_{1}=1^{5}$

and let a meiosis with the strand asymmetry be the prefix–suffix
operation

$g_{k}(a,b)=a[1:k]\,b[k+1:5],\qquad 0\le k\le5$.

With one obligatory crossover the $F_{1}\to F_{2}$ gamete pool is the
monotone $0^{*}1^{*}$ set

${\cal H}_{1}=\{ s_{k}=0^{k}1^{5-k}:0\le k\le5\}$,

$|{\cal H}_{1}|=6$, the six $F_{2}$ chromatids.  Let $s_{i}=0^{i}1^{5-i}$,
$s_{j}=0^{j}1^{5-j}\in{\cal H}_{1}$ be the two $F_{2}$ homologues and let
the $F_{2}\to F_{3}$ meiosis cut at $k$.  On the fixed positive strand

$R_{ijk}(t)=s_{i}(t),\;t\le k;\qquad R_{ijk}(t)=s_{j}(t),\;t>k$,

i.e. with $a=\min(i,k)$, $b=k-a$, $c=\max(0,j-k)$

$R_{ijk}=0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{5-k-c}=0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d}$,
$a+b+c+d=5$,

so every $F_{3}$ chromatid is a $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ word.  In
particular a word can be written as a splice of two monotone blocks
iff it contains at most one $1\to0$ descent.  The monotone,
$1\to0$–free, words are

$N_{0}=n+1=6$, $0^{i}1^{5-i}$.

Let the unique $1\to0$ descent, if it exists, be at $p$, $1\le p\le4$.
The prefix $R[1:p]$ is monotone and ends in $1$ in $p$ ways and the
suffix $R[p+1:5]$ is monotone and starts in $0$ in $5-p$ ways, so

$N_{p}=p\,(5-p)$

words have the descent at $p$.  Hence

$N_{10}= \sum_{p=1}^{4}p(5-p)=4+6+6+4=20$

words with exactly one $1\to0$ descent, i.e. the genuine
$0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d}$ recombinants.  Up to the fixed orientation

$N_{F_{3}}^{\rm hap}=N_{0}+N_{10}=6+20=26$

different positive–strand chromatids can be present in the $F_{3}$
gamete pool, the six $s_{k}$ being the $F_{2}$ set and

$20=\displaystyle\binom{6}{3}$

of them being $0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d}$ with $0\le a<b<c\le5$ and
novel in $F_{3}$.  E.g. the $20$ new words are the $0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}
1^{5-b}$ with $0\le a<k<b\le5$.

In diploid form the $26$ haplotypes give $26^{2}=676$ ordered
maternal/paternal pairs and

$\displaystyle\binom{26+1}{2}=351$

unordered diploid autosomal genotypes in the $F_{3}$ intercross, $6$
of the haplotypes being the parental/ $F_{2}$ monotone set.

Remark on telomeric convention.  With a crossover required to fall
strictly between two scored SNPs, $1\le k\le4$ and $1\le a,b\le4$, the
$F_{1}\to F_{2}$ pool is the four internal monotone haplotypes
$0^{a}1^{5-a},a=1\ldots4$ and the $F_{2}\to F_{3}$ pool is confined to
the $0^{*}1^{*}$ words which start with $0$ and end with $1$.  There
are then $4$ $F_{2}$ haplotypes and the four two–break words
$01011,01001,01101,00101$, i.e. $8$ distinct positive–strand
chromatids, $8\times9/2=36$ unordered diploid autosomes, the usual
internal–only $C(n+g,g)=C(4+2,2)=15$ mosaic upper bound being
$5$ monotone $+$ $10$ two–break positive-strand haplotypes.  The
$26$–haplotype, $351$–genotype count above is the $k=0,5$ telomeric
convention normally quoted. ∎
public_text.5:
With the two founders written on the arbitrarily chosen strand as

* $P_{0}=0^{5},\qquad P_{1}=1^{5}$

and the orientation fixed so that a meiosis is the left–right splice

$g_{i,j,k}=h_{i}[1:k]\,h_{j}[k+1:5]$,

the $F_{1}\to F_{2}$ gametes are the monotone $0^{*}1^{*}$ words

${\cal H}_{1}=\{ s_{k}=0^{k}1^{5-k}:0\le k\le 5\}$ ,

$|{\cal H}_{1}|=6$, $s_{0}=11111$, $s_{5}=00000$ the two founders.
Let $s_{i},s_{j}\in{\cal H}_{1}$ be the two homologues carried by an
$F_{2}$ plant and let the $F_{2}\to F_{3}$ cross–over be at $k$.
On the fixed strand

$R_{ijk}=s_{i}[1:k]\,s_{j}[k+1:5]
      =0^{a}1^{\,k-a}0^{\,c}1^{\,5-k-c}$,
$a=\min(i,k),\;c=\max(0,j-k)$,

i.e. up to the fixed orientation an $F_{3}$ chromatid is a binary word of
length $5$ of the form

$0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d}, \qquad a+b+c+d=5,\;a,b,c,d\ge0,$

so that $a_{10}\le1$, at most one $1\to0$ descent.  The $1\to0$ free
words are the $6$ monotone $0^{i}1^{5-i}$.  For a unique descent at
$k$, $1\le k\le4$, the left $k$ block can be chosen in $k$ ways and the
right $5-k$ block in $5-k$ ways.  Hence

$N_{k}=k\,(5-k)$

words with the descent at $k$ and

$N_{10}=\sum_{k=1}^{4}k(5-k)=4+6+6+4=20$

words with exactly one $1\to0$ descent.  Together with the six monotone
words

$N_{F3}=N_{1}+N_{10}=6+20=26$

different positive-strand haplotypes can be made by two successive
obligatory single cross-overs in the fixed orientation.  The six
$0^{*}1^{*}$ words

$11111,01111,00111,00011,00001,00000$

are the $F_{2}$ pool and the $20$ words

$0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{\,b-k}1^{5-b},\qquad 0\le a<k<b\le5 $

i.e. $10111,10011,10001,10000,11011,11001,11000,01011,01001,01000,
11101,11100,01101,01100,00101,00100,11110,01110,00110,00010$,
are the genuinely new $F_{3}$ recombinants.  In particular the six
$2^{5}-26$ words containing two $1\to0$ descents, $01010,10101$ etc.,
are never made with the strand asymmetry fixed.

Hence there are $26$ distinct positive-strand chromatid sequences in
$F_{3}$, $6$ of them $F_{2}$-type and $20$ novel $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$
sequences.  In ordered diploid notation this is $26^{2}=676$ ordered
maternal/paternal pairs and $\binom{26+1}{2}=351$ unordered diploid
autosomes.  If the two telomeric cuts $k=0,5$ are discarded as
non-recombinant the internal-only pool is the $4$ internal $F_{2}$
haplotypes $0^{a}1^{5-a},1\le a\le4$ and the four two-break $F_{3}$
haplotypes $01011,01001,01101,00101$, i.e. $8$ positive-strand
haplotypes, $36$ unordered diploid autosomes, the usual $C(4+2,2)=15$
positive-strand bound being recovered when the parental $0^{5},1^{5}$
words are reinstated.  This is the $6+\binom{6}{3}=26$ $a_{10}\le1$
count, $20$ novel $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ haplotypes up to the six
$F_{2}$ monotone words. ∎
public_text.7:
On the arbitrarily chosen strand write the two founders as
$A=0^{5}$ and $B=1^{5}$ and, with the strand asymmetry fixed, put

$$R_{k}(X,Y)=X[1:k]Y[k+1:5],\qquad 0\le k\le5 ,$$

for the gamete which is transmitted on the positive strand.
The $F_{1}\to F_{2}$ gamete pool is therefore

$$S_{1}=\{s_{i}=0^{i}1^{5-i}:0\le i\le5\},$$
$|S_{1}|=6$, the six monotone $0^{*}1^{*}$ words.  The two parental
words are $s_{0}=1^{5}$ and $s_{5}=0^{5}$.

Let $a=s_{i},\,b=s_{j}\in S_{1}$ be the two homologues of an $F_{2}$
individual and let the $F_{2}\to F_{3}$ meiosis cut at $k$.  On the
fixed orientation

$$R_{k}(a,b)=a[1:k]b[k+1:5]
          =0^{a'}1^{k-a'}0^{c}1^{5-k-c},$$
$$a'=\min(i,k),\qquad c=\max(0,j-k),$$
i.e. every $F_{3}$ chromatid is a $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ word

$$0^{p_{1}}1^{p_{2}}0^{p_{3}}1^{p_{4}},\qquad p_{1}+p_{2}+p_{3}+p_{4}=5,
\;p_{i}\ge0,$$

with at most one $1\to0$ descent $a_{10}\le1$.  The monotone words are
the six $s_{i}$.  Let the unique $1\to0$ descent, if it exists, be at
$p$, $1\le p\le4$.  The $p$-prefix can be chosen in $p$ ways as a
monotone word ending in $1$ and the $5-p$ suffix in $5-p$ ways as a
monotone word beginning in $0$.  Hence

$$N_{p}=p\,(5-p)$$

words with the descent at $p$ and

$$N_{10}=\sum_{p=1}^{4}p(5-p)=4+6+6+4=20$$

$0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ words with exactly one $1\to0$ descent.
With the six monotone $0^{*}1^{*}$ words

$$N_{F3}=6+N_{10}=6+20=26$$

different positive-strand chromatids can be made by two obligatory
single-crossover meioses in the fixed orientation.  The six monotone
words are the $F_{2}$ haplotypes $s_{i}$ and the $20$ words

$$0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b},\qquad0\le a<k<b\le5, $$

are the genuinely new $F_{3}$ recombinants, $20=\binom{6}{3}$.  In
particular there are $6$ $F_{2}$-type haplotypes and $20$ novel
$F_{3}$ haplotypes on the arbitrarily chosen strand.

In diploid terms the $26$ haplotypes give
$26^{2}=676$ ordered maternal/paternal pairs and

$$\binom{26+1}{2}=351$$

unordered diploid autosomal genotypes in the $F_{3}$ intercross, the
$6$ monotone haplotypes corresponding to the $F_{2}$ gametes.

Remark.  With the usual internal-only convention $1\le k\le4$ the two
parental telomeric products $k=0,5$ are removed.  The $F_{1}\to F_{2}$
pool is then the four internal recombinants $0^{i}1^{5-i}$, $1\le i\le4$,
and the $F_{2}\to F_{3}$ pool on the fixed strand is

$$01111,00111,00011,00001,01011,01001,01101,00101,$$

$4$ monotone + $4$ $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ $=8$ distinct positive-strand
haplotypes, i.e. $8^{2}=64$ ordered and $\binom{8+1}{2}=36$ unordered
diploid autosomes, the $4$ new $F_{3}$ haplotypes $01011,01001,01101,
00101$ usually quoted.  This is the $8\to36$ internal-only version of
the $26\to351$ count above. ∎
public_text.1:
On the $+$ strand write the two inbred founders as

$$P_{0}=0^{5},\qquad P_{1}=1^{5}$$

and put for a crossover after $k$ markers

$$R_{k}(X,Y)=X[1:k]\,Y[k+1:5],\qquad 0\le k\le5 .$$

In the fixed left$\,\to\,$right orientation a $P_{0}/P_{1}$ meiosis can
only give the monotone $0\to1$ words

$$S_{1}=\{s_{i}=0^{i}1^{5-i}\;:\;0\le i\le5\},\qquad |S_{1}|=6,  $$

$11111,01111,00111,00011,00001,00000$, the $F_{1}\to F_{2}$ gamete pool.
Let $s_{i},s_{j}\in S_{1}$ be the two $F_{2}$ homologues.  With the
same fixed orientation the $F_{2}\to F_{3}$ gamete is

$$g_{ij k}=s_{i}[1:k]\,s_{j}[k+1:5] .$$

Writing $i<k<j$ the non-trivial splice is

$$g_{ijk}=0^{i}1^{\,k-i}0^{\,j-k}1^{\,5-j}
       =0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d},\qquad a+b+c+d=5,$$

i.e. a word with at most one $1\to0$ descent, a $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$
word.  For $i\ge k$ or $j\le k$ the splice collapses to a monotone
$s_{p}=0^{p}1^{5-p}$.  Hence on the chosen $+$ strand a $F_{3}$ chromatin
is a word

$$0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d},\qquad a+b+c+d=5,\;a,b,c,d\ge0,  $$

and $a_{10}\le1$.  The monotone $a_{10}=0$ class is

$$N_{1}=5+1=6,\qquad s_{i}=0^{i}1^{5-i}, $$

the $F_{2}$ haplotypes.  A word with exactly one $1\to0$ descent is
fixed by the position $p$ of the descent, $1\le p\le4$, the $p$-prefix
being a monotone word ending in $1$ and the $5-p$ suffix being a
monotone word starting in $0$.  The number of words with the descent
at $p$ is $p(5-p)$ and

$$N_{10}=\sum_{p=1}^{4}p(5-p)=4+6+6+4=20 .$$

Hence

$$N_{+}=N_{1}+N_{10}=6+\binom{6}{3}=6+20=26$$

different $+$ strand chromatids can be present in the $F_{3}$ gamete
pool.  Six of them are the $F_{2}$ monotone haplotypes
$0^{i}1^{5-i}$, $0\le i\le5$, and

$$N_{{\rm new}}=\binom{6}{3}=20$$

of them are genuinely new $F_{3}$ $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ haplotypes,
$0\le a<k<j\le5$, e.g. $0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{j-k}1^{5-j}$.  The $20$ triples
$a<k<j$ are the $20$ novel recombinant $+$ strand sequences; with the
six $F_{2}$ monotone types in the background there are $26$ distinct
single-chromosome $+$ strand sequences in $F_{3}$.

In diploid terms the $26$ haplotypes give $26^{2}=676$ ordered
maternal/paternal pairs and

$$\binom{26+1}{2}=351$$

unordered diploid autosomal genotypes in $F_{3}$.  Up to the
conventional internal-only convention $k=1\ldots4$ the $F_{1}\to F_{2}$
pool is the four internal recombinants $0^{a}1^{5-a}$, $1\le a\le4$, and
the $F_{2}\to F_{3}$ $+$ strand pool is the $4$ monotone $F_{2}$ types
together with the $4$ two-break types $01011,01001,01101,00101$, i.e.
$8$ distinct $+$ strand chromatids, $8^{2}=64$ ordered and
$8\cdot9/2=36$ unordered diploid autosomes, the usual $C(4+2,2)=15$
$0\!-\!1$ mosaic count with the two parental telomeric haplotypes
removed.  This is the $6+\binom63$ $a_{10}\le1$ count usually quoted as
the $F_{3}$ diversity with the fixed orientation. ∎
public_text.2:
On the strand which is followed by the asymmetric exchange a one–crossover
meiosis is the prefix–suffix splice

$$R_{k}(a,b)=a[1\!:\!k]\,b[k+1\!:\!5] ,\qquad 0\le k\le 5 ,$$

and with the two founders $P_{0}=0^{5}$ and $P_{1}=1^{5}$,

$$H_{1}(i)=0^{i}1^{\,5-i},\qquad 0\le i\le 5 ,$$

is the whole $F_{1}\!\to\!F_{2}$ gamete pool.  Put $a=H_{1}(i)$,
$b=H_{1}(j)$ in an $F_{2}$ heterozygote and let the second $F_{2}\!\to\!F_{3}$
meiosis cut at $k$.  On the positive strand

\begin{equation*}
R_{ijk}=H_{1}(i)[1\!:\!k]\,H_{1}(j)[k+1\!:\!5]
      =0^{\min(i,k)}1^{\,k-\min(i,k)}
        0^{\max(0,j-k)}1^{\,5-k-\max(0,j-k)} ,
\end{equation*}
i.e. up to the fixed orientation every $F_{3}$ chromatid is a
$0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ word

$$w=0^{p_{1}}1^{p_{2}}0^{p_{3}}1^{p_{4}},\qquad p_{1}+p_{2}+p_{3}+p_{4}=5,
\;p_{i}\ge0,$$

with at most one $1\to0$ descent.  The $1\to0$–free words are the
$5+1$ monotone words

$$N_{1}=6,\qquad 0^{i}1^{\,5-i}\;, $$

which are the whole $F_{2}$ pool $00000,00001,00011,00111,01111,11111$.
Let the unique $1\to0$ descent be at $k$, $1\le k\le4$.  The $k$-prefix
must be monotone and end in $1$ and the $5-k$ suffix must be monotone
and begin in $0$, so that for the fixed $k$

$$N_{k}=k\,(5-k)$$

different words have their unique descent at $k$.  Hence

$$N_{10}= \sum_{k=1}^{4}k(5-k)=4+6+6+4=20$$

words with exactly one $1\to0$ descent, e.g.

$$00101,01101,01001,01011,00110,01110,\dots$$

so that on the arbitrarily chosen positive strand

$$N_{F_{3}}=N_{1}+N_{10}=6+20=26$$

different single-chromosome haplotypes can be present in the $F_{3}$
gamete pool, $6$ of them being the $F_{1}$–type monotone
$0^{*}1^{*}$ haplotypes and $20$ of them being the genuine
$0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ $F_{3}$ recombinants.  In particular there are
$20$ strictly novel positive-strand haplotypes created in the
$F_{2}\to F_{3}$ meiosis, the six monotone $0^{i}1^{5-i}$ being already
present in $F_{2}$.

In diploid notation the $26$ haplotypes give $26^{2}=676$ ordered
maternal/paternal genotypes and

$$\binom{26+1}{2}=351$$

unordered diploid autosomal genotypes in the $F_{3}$.  The $20$
$0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ words are the $ \binom{6}{3}=20$ new
positive-strand mosaics usually quoted as the $F_{3}$ contribution; with
the conventional internal–only $1\le k\le4$ convention the internal
positive-strand pool is the four $F_{2}$ haplotypes $0^{a}1^{5-a}$,
$1\le a\le4$, together with the four two-break haplotypes
$01011,01001,01101,00101$, i.e. eight distinct positive-strand
chromatids, $36$ unordered diploids. ∎

5.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The two inbred founders on the arbitrarily chosen positive strand are $P_{0}=0^{5}$ and $P_{1}=1^{5}$. With the strand asymmetry fixed the $F_{1}\to F_{2}$ meiosis is the left-to-right splice $R_{k}(X,Y)=X[1:k]Y[k+1:5]$, $0\le k\le5$, giving the monotone $0\to1$ set
$S_{1}=\{s_{i}=0^{i}1^{5-i}:0\le i\le5\}$, $|S_{1}|=6$, the $F_{2}$ haplotype pool.

An $F_{2}\to F_{3}$ gamete from $s_{i},s_{j}\in S_{1}$ with cut $k$ is
$g_{ijk}=s_{i}[1:k]s_{j}[k+1:5]=0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d}$ with $a+b+c+d=5$, i.e. a binary word of length 5 with at most one $1\to0$ descent, $a_{10}\le1$, the $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ form.

Monotone $a_{10}=0$ words: $N_{1}=6$. For a unique descent at $p$, $1\le p\le4$, prefix monotone ending in 1 has $p$ choices and suffix monotone starting in 0 has $5-p$ choices, so $N_{p}=p(5-p)$. 
$N_{10}= \sum_{p=1}^{4}p(5-p)=4+6+6+4=20$.

Hence on the fixed positive strand
$N_{+}=N_{1}+N_{10}=6+20=26$ distinct chromatids can appear in $F_{3}$, $6$ monotone $F_{2}$-type and $20$ genuinely new $0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d}$ with $0\le a<k<b\le5$, i.e. $6+\binom{6}{3}=26$. The $20$ novel words are the $0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b}$ triples; the $2^{5}-26=6$ words with two $10$ descents e.g. $01010,10101$ are unattainable with fixed orientation.

Diploid consequences: $26^{2}=676$ ordered maternal/paternal pairs, $\binom{26+1}{2}=351$ unordered diploid autosomes.

Internal-only convention. If cuts are required strictly between scored SNPs, $1\le k\le4$ and $1\le a,b\le4$, the $F_{1}\to F_{2}$ pool reduces to the four internal monotone haplotypes $0^{a}1^{5-a}$, $1\le a\le4$. Then the positive-strand $F_{3}$ pool is $4$ monotone $+$ $4$ two-break words $01011,01001,01101,00101$, i.e. $8$ distinct chromatids, $8^{2}=64$ ordered and $\binom{8+1}{2}=36$ unordered diploid autosomes. This is the $C(4+2,2)=15$ mosaic bound with telomeric loci re-instated.

Current round 1 consensus is unanimous for the telomeric-allowed fixed-orientation count $26$ haplotypes / $351$ unordered diploids, $20$ novel $F_{3}$ haplotypes on top of the six $F_{2}$ monotone types. The remaining ambiguity is whether the question asks for haploid chromatid count $26$ vs diploid autosome count $351$ $/$ $676$, and whether telomeric $k=0,5$ cuts are to be counted. Round-0 disagreement about $8$ vs $11$ vs $22$ vs $26$/$30$ is now resolved in favour of the $6+\binom{6}{3}=26$ $a_{10}\le1$ count under the usual telomeric convention with fixed orientation; the $8$-haplotype $36$-genotype internal-only variant is the recognized strict-internal alternative.

6.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The five SNP positive strand can be encoded 0 = strain A, 1 = strain B. With one obligatory crossover per meiosis and the strand asymmetry fixed, a meiosis is the left-to-right splice
R_k(X,Y)=X[1:k]Y[k+1:5], 0≤k≤5. 
F1→F2 gametes are the monotone 0*1* words
s_i = 0^{i}1^{5-i}, 0≤i≤5, |S1|=6.

For an F2 heterozygote s_i/s_j with cut k the F2→F3 gamete on the fixed + strand is
g_{ijk}=s_i[1:k]s_j[k+1:5]=0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d}, a+b+c+d=5,
a= min(i,k), b=k-a, c=max(0,j-k), d=5-k-c. Hence every F3 chromatid is a 0*1*0*1* word with at most one 1→0 descent, a_{10}≤1.

Monotone a_{10}=0 class: N0 = n+1 =6, the F2 set 00000,00001,00011,00111,01111,11111.

Words with exactly one 1→0 descent at position p, 1≤p≤4, have p choices for a monotone prefix ending in 1 and 5-p choices for a monotone suffix beginning in 0, N_p = p(5-p). 
N10 = Σ_{p=1}^{4} p(5-p)=4+6+6+4=20.

Hence on the arbitrarily chosen positive strand with telomeric cuts k=0,5 allowed

|H_F3^+| = N0+N10 =6+20=26

distinct haploid chromatids, the six monotone F2 types and 20 = C(6,3) genuinely new 0*1*0*1* recombinants of the form 0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b} with 0≤a<k<b≤5. The 2^5-26=6 words with two 1→0 descents e.g. 01010,10101 and shifts, are unattainable with fixed orientation.

Diploid counting from the 26 haploid types: ordered maternal/paternal pairs 26^2=676, unordered diploid autosomes C(26+1,2)=351.

Convention dependence noted throughout the discussion:
* Telomeric inclusive k=0,5 is the 26/351 count above.
* Internal-only convention 1≤k≤4 and 1≤i,j≤4 removes the parental telomeric words. Then F1→F2 pool is the four internal monotone 0^{a}1^{5-a}, a=1..4, and F2→F3 yields the four monotone + four two-break words 01011,01001,01101,00101, i.e. 8 distinct + strand chromatids, 8^2=64 ordered, C(8+1,2)=36 unordered diploid autosomes. This is the textbook C(4+2,2)=15 mosaic bound with parental words reinstated.
* Allowing the reciprocal orientation doubles the BABA family and gives the familiar 30-word ≤3-switch bound.

Current belief is stable: with the usual telomeric-inclusive definition the positive-strand haploid diversity in F3 is 26, 20 strictly novel 0*1*0*1* recombinants on top of the 6 F2 monotone haplotypes, 351 unordered diploid genotypes. The internal-only strictly recombinant version quoted in many textbooks is the 8 haploid / 36 diploid statement.

4.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The two founders on the chosen positive strand are $P0=0^5$ and $P1=1^5$. With the fixed left→right splice $R_k(X,Y)=X[1:k]Y[k+1:5]$ the $F1\to F2$ gamete pool is the monotone $0^{*}1^{*}$ set

${\cal H}_1=\{s_i=0^{i}1^{5-i}:0\le i\le5\}$, $|{\cal H}_1|=6$,

$11111,01111,00111,00011,00001,00000$.

s_i=0^i1^{5-i}, 0≤i≤5. |S1|=6 monotone 0*1* haplotypes, the F2 pool.

An F2 individual carries s_i=0^i1^{5-i} and s_j=0^j1^{5-j}. With a second one-way cut at k the F3 gamete is s_i[1:k]s_j[k+1:5]. Hence on the fixed orientation every attainable word is 0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d} with a+b+c+d=5, i.e. a binary word of length 5 with at most one 1→0 descent, a10≤1.

Monotone a10=0 : N1=n+1=6.
Exactly one 1→0 descent at position p,1≤p≤4, prefix can be chosen in p ways, suffix in 5-p ways → Np=p(5-p). 
N10 = Σ p(5-p)=4+6+6+4=20.
Hence per chromatid on the fixed orientation N_F3 =6+20=26 distinct positive-strand haplotypes, 6 monotone F2 types and 20 0*1*0*1* novel F3 types. Closed form N(n)=n+1+n(n-1)(n+1)/6, N(5)=26. The 20 novel are 0^a1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b} with 0≤a<k<b≤5, e.g. 01011,01001,01101,00101 etc. The 2^5-26=6 words with two 1→0 descents, in particular 01010 and 10101, are unattainable with fixed orientation and two single-crossover meioses.

Diploid consequences from the 26 haplotypes: 26^2=676 ordered maternal/paternal pairs and C(26+1,2)=351 unordered diploid autosomes. Six monotone haplotypes correspond to the F2 gamete pool.

Variants noted:
* Internal-only convention k=1..4, a,b∈{1..4} : F2 pool is the four internal 0^a1^{5-a}. Then attainable positive-strand chromatids that start with 0 are 4 monotone +4 two-break =8 haplotypes per chromatid, 8^2=64 ordered, C(8+1,2)=36 unordered. This is the usual C(n+g,g)=C(4+2,2)=15 0-1 mosaics with telomeric formal loci restored.
* Up to reciprocal 1↔0 complement the textbook bound is 2 Σ_{k=0}^2 C4k =30 words with ≤3 switches, 22 reciprocal-counted words, 11 essentially different 0→1 types. The 26→30 difference is the BABA family recovered when reciprocal orientation is allowed.

Current round consensus is uniform: 26 positive-strand haplotypes, 20 genuinely new F3 recombinants on top of the six F2 monotone types. Remaining disagreement is purely definitional – whether telomeric k=0,5 cuts are counted as biologically distinct recombinants or excluded as internal-only; that changes the per-chromatid number from 26 to 8 strictly internal, 15 with telomeric formal loci. No material dispute on the a10≤1 counting.
reflection_text.1:
The two founders on the + strand can be taken as $A=0^{5},\,B=1^{5}$.
With the strand asymmetry a meiosis is the left-right splice 
$h_{1}\xrightarrow{k}h_{1}[1\!:\!k]\,h_{2}[k+1\!:\!5]$, $k=0\ldots5$.
$F_{1}\!\to\!F_{2}$ therefore gives the monotone set 
$S_{1}=\{s_i=0^{i}1^{5-i}:0\le i\le5\}$, $|S_{1}|=6$.
An $F_{2}$ individual carries $s_i,s_j\in S_{1}$ and an $F_{2}\!\to\!F_{3}$ 
gamete is $s_i[1\!:\!k]\,s_j[k+1\!:\!5]$.

For $0<i<k<j$
$s_i[1\!:\!k]\,s_j[k+1\!:\!5]=0^{i}1^{\,k-i}0^{\,j-k}1^{\,5-j}
      =0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d}$,
$a=i,\;b=k-i>0,\;c=j-k>0,\;d=5-j$, $a+b+c+d=5$, i.e. a word with
at most one $1\to0$ descent, $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$.  If $i\ge k$ or $j\le k$
the splice collapses to a monotone $0^{p}1^{5-p}$.

Hence with $k$ allowed $0\ldots5$ the attainable + strand words are exactly
the $0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d}$ with $a+b+c+d=5$.  The non-monotone words are in
bijection with increasing triples $0\le i<k<j\le5$,

$N_{nm}= \binom{6}{3}=20$,

and with the six monotone words

$N_{+}=6+20=26$,

$6$ $F_{2}$-type $0^{*}1^{*}$ haplotypes and $20$ $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$
$F_{3}$ haplotypes.  $N(n)=n+1+n(n-1)(n+1)/6$, $N(5)=26$,
$N_{10}=\sum_{p=1}^{4}p(5-p)=20$. The six monotone words are the $F_{2}$
haplotypes $s_i$, the 20 words $0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{j-k}1^{5-j}$ with
$0\le a<k<j\le5$ are the genuinely new $F_{3}$ chromatids.

In diploid notation this is $26^{2}=676$ ordered and
$\binom{26+1}{2}=351$ unordered $F_{3}$ autosomes. The $20$ novel
$0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ haplotypes are the $20=\binom63$ strictly new
positive-strand recombinants; the six monotone $0^{*}1^{*}$ haplotypes are
already present in $F_{2}$.

Internal-only convention $1\le k\le4$, $1\le a,b\le4$: $F_{1}\to F_{2}$
pool is the four internal $0^{a}1^{5-a}$, $1\le a\le4$, and the
$F_{2}\to F_{3}$ + strand pool is $4$ monotone + $4$ two-break
$01011,01001,01101,00101$, i.e. $8$ distinct + strand chromatids,
$8^{2}=64$ ordered, $\binom{8+1}{2}=36$ unordered diploid autosomes,
the usual $C(4+2,2)=15$ $0\!-\!1$ mosaic count with telomeres removed.
The $2^{5}-26=6$ words with two $1\to0$ descents, e.g. $01010,10101$,
are unattainable with the fixed orientation and two single-crossover
meioses. The consensus of the round is the $6+\binom63=26$ + strand
haplotype bound, $20$ novel recombinant haplotypes on top of the six
$F_{2}$ monotone types.
