reflection_text.7:
The five SNPs are 0=B on the positive strand and 1=A on the positive strand. With strand asymmetry fixed the meiosis operation on two homologues a,b is R_k(a,b)=a[1:k] b[k+1:5], 0≤k≤5. F1→F2 gamete pool is the monotone 0*1* set S1={0^i1^{5-i}:0≤i≤5}, |S1|=6, the six F2 haplotypes.

Let a=s_i, b=s_j∈S1 be the two homologues of an F2 individual and cut at k. On the fixed orientation

R_ijk =0^{a'}1^{k-a'}0^{c}1^{5-k-c}, a'=min(i,k), c=max(0,j-k),

so every F3 gamete is 0^{p1}1^{p2}0^{p3}1^{p4}, p1+p2+p3+p4=5, i.e. a word with at most one 1→0 descent, a10≤1. Monotone a10=0 words are N1=n+1=6. A word with a unique 1→0 descent at p,1≤p≤4, has p choices for the monotone prefix ending in 1 and 5-p choices for the monotone suffix starting in 0, Np=p(5-p). Hence N10=∑_{p=1}^{4}p(5-p)=4+6+6+4=20. 

N_F3^{+}=N1+N10=6+20=26 distinct positive-strand chromatids attainable by two obligatory single-crossover meioses with orientation fixed. Six are the F2 monotone s_i, 20= C(6,3) are the genuinely new 0*1*0*1* haplotypes 0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b} with 0≤a<k<b≤5. The six words with two 1→0 descents, 2^5−26=6, are unattainable.

Diploid: 26^2=676 ordered maternal/paternal pairs, unordered = C(26+1,2)=351 autosomal genotypes.

Internal-only convention 1≤k≤4, 1≤a,b≤4 removes telomeric k=0,5 and parental 0^5,1^5: F1→F2 pool is the four internal monotone 0^a1^{5-a}, a=1..4, and F2→F3 gives four two-break words 01011,01001,01101,00101. Hence 4 monotone +4 recombinant =8 distinct positive-strand chromatids, 8^2=64 ordered, C(8+1,2)=36 unordered diploid autosomes, the usual 8→36 internal-only statement. This is the C(n+g,g)=C(4+2,2)=15 mosaic bound with telomeric products removed.

All eight colleagues in round 1 converge on the 26-haplotype / 20-novel / 351-unordered diploid count with the fixed-orientation 0*1*0*1* description; the 8-haplotype /36-genotype version is the conventional internal-only telomeric-excluded variant. No new disagreement appeared; the a10≤1 formula N(n)=n+1+n(n-1)(n+1)/6 gives 26 for n=5.
reflection_text.2:
The problem is the set of binary words of length 5 that can be made by two successive obligatory single-crossover meioses with the left→right order fixed on the arbitrarily chosen positive strand.

Founders on the + strand are $0^{5}$ and $1^{5}$. With the fixed orientation a meiosis is the prefix-suffix splice $R_{k}(X,Y)=X[1:k]Y[k+1:5]$, $0\le k\le5$. 
$F_{1}\to F_{2}$ therefore gives the monotone $0^{*}1^{*}$ set

$H_{1}(i)=0^{i}1^{5-i}$, $0\le i\le5$, $|H_{1}|=6$, the $F_{2}$ gamete pool.

Let an $F_{2}$ heterozygote carry $s_{i}=0^{i}1^{5-i}$ and $s_{j}=0^{j}1^{5-j}$ and let the $F_{2}\to F_{3}$ cut be $k$.
On the fixed strand

$R_{ijk}=s_{i}[1:k]s_{j}[k+1:5]=0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{c}1^{5-k-c}$,
$a=\min(i,k)$, $c=\max(0,j-k)$,

i.e. every $F_{3}$ chromatid is $0^{p_{1}}1^{p_{2}}0^{p_{3}}1^{p_{4}}$,
$p_{1}+p_{2}+p_{3}+p_{4}=5$, $a_{10}\le1$: at most one $1\to0$ descent.

Monotone $a_{10}=0$ words: $N_{1}=5+1=6$, $0^{i}1^{5-i}$.
A word with a unique $1\to0$ descent at $p$, $1\le p\le4$, has $p$ choices for a monotone prefix ending in $1$ and $5-p$ choices for a monotone suffix beginning in $0$, i.e. $N_{p}=p(5-p)$ words.

$N_{10}=\sum_{p=1}^{4}p(5-p)=4+6+6+4=20$.
Hence on the fixed + strand

$N_{+}=N_{1}+N_{10}=6+20=26$ distinct single-chromosome haplotypes can be present in $F_{3}$.

The six monotone $s_{i}$ are the $F_{2}$ set; the $20=\binom{6}{3}$ words with $0\le a<k<b\le5$,

$0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b}$, 

are the genuinely new $F_{3}$ $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ recombinants. $2^{5}-26=6$ words with two $1\to0$ descents, e.g. $01010$, $10101$, are unattainable with the fixed orientation.

Diploid: $26^{2}=676$ ordered maternal/paternal pairs, $\binom{26+1}{2}=351$ unordered diploid autosomes. The six monotone haplotypes correspond to the $F_{2}$ pool.

Convention note: with the strict internal-only convention $1\le k\le4$ and $1\le a,b\le4$ the telomeric $k=0,5$ products $0^{5},1^{5}$ are removed. Then the positive-strand pool is the four internal $F_{2}$ haplotypes $0^{a}1^{5-a}$, $1\le a\le4$, plus the four two-break words $01011,01001,01101,00101$, i.e. $8$ distinct + strand chromatids, $8^{2}=64$ ordered and $\binom{8+1}{2}=36$ unordered diploid autosomes, the usual $C(4+2,2)=15$ mosaic upper bound up to orientation. All eight colleagues in round 1 converge on the $6+20=26$ telomere-inclusive count, $20$ strictly novel $F_{3}$ haplotypes, with the internal-only $8$/$36$ variant as a footnote.

1.text:
On the chosen $+$ strand the two founders can be written

$P_{0}=0^{5}$ , $P_{1}=1^{5}$

and with the fixed left$\to$right asymmetry a meiosis is the prefix
suffix splice

$R_{k}(X,Y)=X[1:k]Y[k+1:5],\qquad 0\le k\le5$.

$F_{1}\to F_{2}$ therefore gives the monotone $0^{*}1^{*}$ set

${\cal H}_{1}=\{s_{i}=0^{i}1^{5-i}:0\le i\le5\}$ , 
$|{\cal H}_{1}|=6$,

$11111,01111,00111,00011,00001,00000$, the whole $F_{2}$ gamete pool on
the $+$ strand.

Let $s_{i},s_{j}\in{\cal H}_{1}$ be the two $F_{2}$ homologues and let the
$F_{2}\to F_{3}$ cut be $k$. On the fixed orientation

$g_{ijk}=s_{i}[1:k]\,s_{j}[k+1:5]=0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d}$,
$a+b+c+d=5$,

i.e. a $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ word with at most one $1\to0$ descent.
For $i\ge k$ or $j\le k$ the splice collapses to a monotone $s_{p}$;
for $0<i<k<j$

$g_{ijk}=0^{i}1^{\,k-i}0^{\,j-k}1^{\,5-j}$,

so that up to the fixed orientation every $F_{3}$ chromatid is
$0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d}$ with $a_{10}\le1$.

The $1\to0$ free words are

$N_{1}=n+1=6$, $0^{i}1^{5-i}$,
the $F_{2}$ haplotypes.  Let the unique $1\to0$ descent be at $p$,
$1\le p\le4$.  The $p$-prefix can be chosen in $p$ ways as a monotone
word ending in $1$ and the $5-p$ suffix in $5-p$ ways as a monotone word
beginning in $0$, so

$N_{p}=p(5-p)$

words have the descent at $p$ and

$N_{10}= \sum_{p=1}^{4}p(5-p)=4+6+6+4=20$

words have exactly one $1\to0$ descent.  Hence on the arbitrarily chosen
$+$ strand

$N_{+}=N_{1}+N_{10}=6+20=6+\binom{6}{3}=26$

different single chromosome haplotypes can be present in the $F_{3}$
gamete pool.  Six of them are the $F_{2}$ monotone $0^{*}1^{*}$ types
$s_{i}=0^{i}1^{5-i}$, $0\le i\le5$, and

$N_{\rm new}= \binom{6}{3}=20$

of them are genuinely new $F_{3}$ $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ haplotypes,
$0\le a<k<j\le5$, e.g. $0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{j-k}1^{5-j}$.  The $2^{5}-26=6$
words with two $1\to0$ descents, $01010$ etc., are unattainable with the
fixed orientation and two obligatory single cross-overs.

In diploid notation the $26$ $+$ strand haplotypes give $26^{2}=676$
ordered maternal/paternal pairs and

$\displaystyle \binom{26+1}{2}=351$

unordered diploid autosomal genotypes in $F_{3}$, $6$ haplotypes being
the $F_{2}$ pool and $20$ the novel $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ $F_{3}$
recombinants.  With the conventional internal-only $1\le k\le4$ convention
the telomeric $k=0,5$ products are removed, leaving the $4$ internal
$F_{2}$ monotone types and the four two-break types
$01011,01001,01101,00101$, i.e. $8$ distinct $+$ strand chromatids and
$8\cdot9/2=36$ unordered diploid autosomes, the $4$ novel $F_{3}$
haplotypes usually quoted. ∎

4.text:
On the chosen strand put the two inbred founders

$P_{0}=0^{5}$ , $P_{1}=1^{5}$ 

and with the strand asymmetry write a meiosis as the left-to-right
prefix–suffix splice

$R_{k}(X,Y)=X[1:k]Y[k+1:5],\qquad 0\le k\le5 $ .

$F_{1}\to F_{2}$.  $R_{k}(P_{0},P_{1})=0^{k}1^{5-k}$ and $R_{k}(P_{1},P_{0})
=1^{k}0^{5-k}$ in the two orientations.  On the fixed $+$ strand the
$F_{1}\!\to\!F_{2}$ gamete pool is therefore the monotone

${\cal H}_{1}=\{s_{i}=0^{i}1^{5-i}\;:\;0\le i\le5\}$ , $|{\cal H}_{1}|=6$,

$11111,01111,00111,00011,00001,00000$, the $0^{*}1^{*}$ $F_{2}$ haplotypes.

$F_{2}\to F_{3}$.  Let $s_{i}=0^{i}1^{5-i},\,s_{j}=0^{j}1^{5-j}\in{\cal H}_{1}$
be the two $F_{2}$ homologues and let the second obligatory crossover be
at $k$.  On the fixed $+$ strand

$g_{ijk}=s_{i}[1:k]s_{j}[k+1:5]
      =0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d},\qquad a+b+c+d=5,\;a,b,c,d\ge0,$

i.e. a $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ word.  In particular $a_{10}\le1$, at most one
$1\to0$ descent.  If $i\ge k$ or $j\le k$ the splice collapses to a
monotone $s_{p}=0^{p}1^{5-p}$.

$a_{10}=0$.  The monotone class is

$N_{1}=5+1=6,\qquad s_{i}=0^{i}1^{5-i},$

the $F_{2}$ pool.

$a_{10}=1$.  Let the unique $1\to0$ descent be at $p$, $1\le p\le4$.
The $p$–prefix must be a monotone word ending in $1$ and can be chosen
in $p$ ways, the $5-p$ suffix must be a monotone word beginning in $0$
and can be chosen in $5-p$ ways.  Hence

$N_{p}=p(5-p)$

words have the descent at $p$ and

$N_{10}=\sum_{p=1}^{4}p(5-p)=4+6+6+4=20$

distinct $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ words with exactly one $1\to0$ descent.
They are the $0\le a<k<b\le5$ splices

$g_{ijk}=0^{a}1^{\,k-a}0^{\,b-k}1^{\,5-b},\qquad0\le a<k<b\le5,$

$20=\binom{6}{3}$ different triples $a<k<b$.  The six
$2^{5}-26$ words with two $1\to0$ descents are unattainable with two
successive one-crossover meioses in the fixed orientation.

Hence on the arbitrarily chosen $+$ strand

$N_{+}=N_{1}+N_{10}=6+20=26$

different single–chromosome haplotypes can occur in $F_{3}$, the six
$0^{i}1^{5-i}$ being the $F_{2}$ monotone set and the $20$ 
$0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d}$, $b>0,c>0$, being genuinely new in $F_{3}$.
In particular there are $20$ strictly novel positive-strand
recombinants in $F_{3}$ on top of the six $F_{2}$ types.

In diploid notation the $26$ haplotypes give $26^{2}=676$ ordered
maternal/paternal pairs and

$\displaystyle\binom{26+1}{2}=351$

unordered diploid autosomal genotypes on the fixed strand, $6$ of the
haplotypes being the $F_{2}$ monotone types.  Discarding the $k=0,5$
telomeric formal cuts the conventional internal-only internal set is the
four internal $F_{2}$ haplotypes $0^{a}1^{5-a},\,1\le a\le4$ together with
the four two-break $F_{3}$ words $01011,01001,01101,00101$, i.e. $8$
positive-strand chromatids, $8\cdot9/2=36$ unordered diploids, the usual
textbook $4+4$ count. ∎

7.text:
On the $+$ strand put $P_{0}=0^{5}$ , $P_{1}=1^{5}$ and with the
asymmetry fixed write a meiosis as the left–right prefix–suffix

$$R_{k}(X,Y)=X[1:k]\,Y[k+1:5],\qquad 0\le k\le 5, $$

on the chosen strand.  The $F_{1}\to F_{2}$ pool is then the monotone

$${\cal H}_{1}=\{s_{i}=0^{i}1^{5-i}:0\le i\le5\},\qquad |{\cal H}_{1}|=6,
$$

$11111,01111,00111,00011,00001,00000$, the six $0^{*}1^{*}$ $F_{2}$
chromatids.

Let $s_{i}=0^{i}1^{5-i}$, $s_{j}=0^{j}1^{5-j}\in{\cal H}_{1}$ be the two
$F_{2}$ homologues and let the $F_{2}\to F_{3}$ cut be $k$.  On the fixed
$+$ strand

$$g_{ijk}=s_{i}[1:k]\,s_{j}[k+1:5]
       =0^{\min(i,k)}1^{\,k-\min(i,k)}0^{\max(0,j-k)}1^{\,5-k-\max(0,j-k)} ,
$$

i.e. up to the fixed orientation

$$g_{ijk}=0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d},\qquad a+b+c+d=5,\;a,b,c,d\ge0, $$

a $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ word with $a_{10}\le1$, at most one $1\to0$
descent.  The $a_{10}=0$ class is the $F_{2}$ monotone set

$$N_{1}=n+1=6,\qquad s_{i}=0^{i}1^{5-i} .$$

Let the unique $1\to0$ descent be at $p$, $1\le p\le4$.  The $p$-prefix
has to be monotone and end in $1$ – $p$ possibilities – and the $5-p$
suffix has to be monotone and begin in $0$ – $5-p$ possibilities – so
that

$$N_{p}=p(5-p)$$

words have the descent at $p$.  Hence

$$N_{10}=\sum_{p=1}^{4}p(5-p)=4+6+6+4=20
      =\binom{6}{3}$$

words have exactly one $1\to0$ descent, $0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{\,b-k}1^{5-b}$,
$0\le a<k<b\le5$, the genuinely new $F_{3}$ $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$
recombinants.  With the six $F_{2}$ monotone words

$$N_{F_{3}}^{+}=N_{1}+N_{10}=6+20=26$$

different $+$ strand chromatids can be made by two obligatory
single-crossover meioses in the fixed orientation.  Six of them are the
$F_{2}$ monotone $0^{i}1^{5-i}$; the $20=\binom{6}{3}$ words
$0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d}$ with $b>0,c>0$ are the strictly novel $F_{3}$
haplotypes. The $2^{5}-26=6$ words with two $1\to0$ descents are
unattainable with the orientation fixed.

In diploid notation the $26$ haplotypes give $26^{2}=676$ ordered
maternal/paternal pairs and

$$\binom{26+1}{2}=351$$

unordered diploid autosomal genotypes in $F_{3}$ on the chosen strand.
Removing the telomeric cuts $k=0,5$, i.e. the conventional internal-only
$1\le k\le4$ convention, the $F_{1}\to F_{2}$ internal pool is the four
$0^{a}1^{5-a},\,1\le a\le4$ and the $F_{2}\to F_{3}$ $+$ strand pool is
the four monotone $F_{2}$ types together with the four two-break types
$01011,01001,01101,00101$, i.e. $8$ distinct $+$ strand chromatids,
$8^{2}=64$ ordered and $\binom{8+1}{2}=36$ unordered diploid autosomes,
the usual $8\to36$ internal-only statement. ∎

8.text:
On the $+$ strand the two inbred founders can be written

$$P_{0}=0^{5},\qquad P_{1}=1^{5}$$

and with the strand asymmetry a one crossover meiosis is the 
prefix–suffix splice

$$R_{k}(X,Y)=X[1:k]Y[k+1:5],\qquad 0\le k\le5 .$$

$F_{1}\to F_{2}$.  With one obligatory crossover

$$ {\cal H}_{1}=\{s_{i}=0^{i}1^{\,5-i}:0\le i\le5\},\qquad |{\cal H}_{1}|=6 ,$$

is the whole $F_{1}\to F_{2}$ gamete pool on the fixed strand,
$11111,01111,00111,00011,00001,00000$, the $0^{*}1^{*}$ monotone words.

$F_{2}\to F_{3}$.  Let $s_{i}=0^{i}1^{5-i}$ and $s_{j}=0^{j}1^{5-j}$ be the
two $F_{2}$ homologues and let the second meiosis cut at $k$.  On the
fixed $+$ strand

$$g_{ijk}=s_{i}[1:k]s_{j}[k+1:5]=0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d},
\qquad a+b+c+d=5,$$
i.e. a length $5$ binary word with at most one $1\to0$ descent,
$a_{10}\le1$, a $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ word.  The $1\to0$-free words are
the six monotone $F_{2}$ types

$$N_{1}=n+1=6,\qquad s_{i}=0^{i}1^{5-i}, $$

and a unique $1\to0$ descent can be placed at $p$, $1\le p\le n-1$.
The $p$-prefix has to be a monotone word ending in $1$ and the
$5-p$ suffix a monotone word beginning in $0$, hence

$$N_{p}=p\,(5-p)$$

words with the descent at $p$.  Hence

$$N_{10}= \sum_{p=1}^{4}p(5-p)=4+6+6+4=20,
$$

$0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ words with exactly one $1\to0$ descent, e.g.
$0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{\,b-k}1^{5-b}$ with $0\le a<k<b\le5$.
In particular the $20=\binom{6}{3}$ words

$$0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{\,b-k}1^{5-b},\qquad 0\le a<k<b\le5, $$

are the strictly novel $F_{3}$ recombinants.  With the six $F_{2}$
monotone types in the background

$$N_{+}=N_{1}+N_{10}=6+20=6+\binom{6}{3}=26$$

different $+$ strand chromatids can be generated by two successive
obligatory one-crossover meioses in the fixed orientation, $6$ of them
the $F_{2}$ $0^{*}1^{*}$ haplotypes and $20$ of them genuinely new
$0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ $F_{3}$ haplotypes.  The $2^{5}-26=6$ words with
two $1\to0$ descents, e.g. $01010$, are unattainable with the strand
asymmetry fixed.

In diploid terms the $26$ haplotypes give $26^{2}=676$ ordered
maternal/paternal pairs and

$$\binom{26+1}{2}=351$$

unordered diploid autosomal genotypes in $F_{3}$, the six monotone
haplotypes being the $F_{2}$ pool.  With the usual internal-only
convention $1\le k\le4$ the telomeric $k=0,5$ products are removed and
the internal $+$ strand pool is the four internal $F_{2}$ types
$0^{a}1^{5-a}$, $1\le a\le4$, together with the four two-break types
$01011,01001,01101,00101$, i.e. $8$ distinct $+$ strand chromatids,
$8^{2}=64$ ordered and $\binom{8+1}{2}=36$ unordered diploid
autosomes, the $4$ novel $F_{3}$ internal haplotypes quoted in the
textbook $C(n+g,g)$ form.  Removing the six $F_{2}$ monotone types the
$20$ novel $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ haplotypes are the $F_{3}$ contribution
on the fixed $+$ strand, $N(n)=n+1+n(n-1)(n+1)/6$, $N(5)=26$. ∎

6.text:
On the arbitrarily chosen strand write the two inbred founders as

$P_{0}=0^{5}\qquad P_{1}=1^{5}$

and with the strand asymmetry fixed let a meiosis be the left to right
prefix–suffix splice

$R_{k}(X,Y)=X[1\!:\!k]\,Y[k+1\!:\!5],\qquad 0\le k\le5 ,$

the obligatory one crossover per gamete.  The $F_{1}\to F_{2}$ gamete
pool is therefore the monotone $0^{*}1^{*}$ set

${\cal H}_{1}=\{s_{i}=0^{i}1^{5-i}:0\le i\le5\},\qquad|{\cal H}_{1}|=6,$

$11111,01111,00111,00011,00001,00000$.
Let $s_{i}=0^{i}1^{5-i}$ and $s_{j}=0^{j}1^{5-j}$ be the two $F_{2}$
homologues and let the $F_{2}\to F_{3}$ cut be $k$.  On the fixed $+$ 
strand

$g_{ijk}=s_{i}[1\!:\!k]\,s_{j}[k+1\!:\!5]
       =0^{\min(i,k)}1^{\,k-\min(i,k)}0^{\max(0,j-k)}1^{\,5-k-\max(0,j-k)}
       =0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d},\qquad a+b+c+d=5,$

so every $F_{3}$ chromatid is a $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ word, i.e. a word
with at most one $1\to 0$ descent $a_{10}\le1$.  The $a_{10}=0$ class is
the $F_{2}$ monotone set

$N_{0}=5+1=6,\qquad s_{i}=0^{i}1^{5-i}.$

Let the unique $1\to0$ descent be at $p$, $1\le p\le4$.  The $p$-prefix
has to be a monotone word ending in $1$ : $p$ possibilities, and the
$5-p$ suffix has to be a monotone word beginning in $0$ : $5-p$
possibilities.  Hence

$N_{p}=p(5-p)$

words have their descent at $p$ and

$N_{10}= \sum_{p=1}^{4}p(5-p)=4+6+6+4=20$

words have exactly one $1\to0$ descent.  In the form
$0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{\,b-k}1^{5-b}$ with $0\le a<k<b\le5$ this is
$\binom{6}{3}=20$ genuinely new $F_{3}$ $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ mosaics.

Hence on the fixed $+$ strand

$N_{F_{3}}^{+}=N_{0}+N_{10}=6+20=26$

different single-chromosome haplotypes can be present in the $F_{3}$
gamete pool, the six $0^{i}1^{5-i}$ being the $F_{2}$ monotone types and
the $20=\binom63$ words $0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d}$ with $b>0,c>0$ being the
strictly novel $F_{3}$ recombinants.  The $2^{5}-26=6$ words with two
$1\to0$ descents, e.g. $01010$, are unattainable with the fixed
orientation and two obligatory single cross-overs.

In diploid notation the $26$ $+$ strand haplotypes give $26^{2}=676$
ordered maternal/paternal pairs and

$\displaystyle\binom{26+1}{2}=351$

unordered diploid autosomal genotypes in $F_{3}$.  The $20$ new
$0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ haplotypes are the $F_{3}$ contribution on top of
the six $F_{2}$ monotone haplotypes.

Remark on convention.  With the usual internal–only convention
$1\le k\le4$ the two telomeric cuts $k=0,5$ are discarded.  The
$F_{1}\to F_{2}$ pool is then the four internal monotone haplotypes
$0^{a}1^{5-a}$, $1\le a\le4$, and the $+$ strand $F_{2}\to F_{3}$ pool
is the four monotone $F_{2}$ types together with the four two-break
types $01011,01001,01101,00101$, i.e. $8$ distinct $+$ strand
chromatids, $8^{2}=64$ ordered and $\binom{8+1}{2}=36$ unordered diploid
autosomes, the textbook $C(4+2,2)=15$ mosaic bound with the parental
telomeric words reinstated.  The $26\to351$ count above is the
$k=0,5$ telomeric inclusive count normally quoted. ∎

5.text:
On the arbitrarily chosen $+$ strand write the two inbred founders as
$P_{0}=0^{5}$ and $P_{1}=1^{5}$ and let a meiosis with the fixed
asymmetry be the prefix–suffix splice

$$R_{k}(X,Y)=X[1:k]Y[k+1:5],\qquad 0\le k\le 5 .$$

$F_{1}\to F_{2}$ is therefore the monotone $0^{*}1^{*}$ set

$${\cal H}_{1}=\{s_{i}=0^{i}1^{5-i}:0\le i\le 5\},\qquad |{\cal H}_{1}|=6,
$$

$11111,01111,00111,00011,00001,00000$.  Let $s_{i},s_{j}\in{\cal H}_{1}$
be the two $F_{2}$ homologues and let the $F_{2}\to F_{3}$ cut be $k$.
On the fixed $+$ strand

$$g_{ijk}=s_{i}[1:k]s_{j}[k+1:5]=0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d},
\qquad a+b+c+d=5, $$

i.e. every $F_{3}$ chromatid is a $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ word with
$a_{10}\le 1$.  The $1\to0$-free words are the six monotone words
$N_{1}=5+1=6$.

Let the unique $1\to0$ descent, if it is present, be at $p$, $1\le p\le4$.
The $p$-prefix has to be a monotone word ending in $1$ and can be chosen
in $p$ ways and the $5-p$ suffix has to be a monotone word beginning
in $0$ and can be chosen in $5-p$ ways, hence

$$N_{p}=p(5-p)$$

words have the descent at $p$ and

$$N_{10}=\sum_{p=1}^{4}p(5-p)=4+6+6+4=20$$

words have exactly one $1\to0$ descent.  Hence on the fixed $+$ strand

$$N_{F_{3}}^{+}=N_{1}+N_{10}=6+20=6+\binom{6}{3}=26$$

different $5$-mer chromatids can be made by two successive obligatory
single cross-overs.  Six of them are the $F_{2}$ monotone types
$0^{i}1^{5-i}$, $0\le i\le5$, and

$$N_{\rm new}=\binom{6}{3}=20$$

of them are genuinely new $F_{3}$ $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ types
$0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{\,b-k}1^{5-b}$ with $0\le a<k<b\le5$, e.g.
$00101,01001,01101,01011,\ldots$.  The $2^{5}-26=6$ words with two
$1\to0$ descents are unattainable with the orientation fixed.

In ordered diploid notation the $26$ $+$ strand haplotypes give
$26^{2}=676$ ordered maternal/paternal pairs and

$$\displaystyle\binom{26+1}{2}=351 $$

unordered diploid autosomal genotypes in $F_{3}$, $20$ novel
haplotypes on top of the six $F_{2}$ monotone haplotypes.

Remark.  With the conventional internal-only convention $1\le k\le4$
the two telomeric $k=0,5$ products are discarded.  The $F_{1}\to F_{2}$
pool is then the four internal monotone haplotypes $0^{a}1^{5-a}$,
$1\le a\le4$, and the $+$ strand $F_{2}\to F_{3}$ pool is the four
monotone $F_{2}$ types together with the four two-break types
$01011,01001,01101,00101$, i.e. $8$ distinct $+$ strand chromatids,
$8^{2}=64$ ordered and $\binom{8+1}{2}=36$ unordered diploid autosomes,
the familiar $C(4+2,2)=15$ mosaic bound with the parental telomeric
haplotypes reinstated. ∎

3.text:
On the $+$ strand put the two inbred founders as

$P_{0}=0^{5},\qquad P_{1}=1^{5}$

and with the one way asymmetry a meiosis is the prefix–suffix splice

$R_{k}(X,Y)=X[1\!:\!k]\,Y[k+1\!:\!5],\qquad 0\le k\le 5$,

on the chosen strand.  For $P_{0}/P_{1}$

${\cal H}_{1}=\{s_{i}=0^{i}1^{5-i}\;:\;0\le i\le5\}$

is the $F_{1}\to F_{2}$ gamete pool, $|{\cal H}_{1}|=6$,

$11111,01111,00111,00011,00001,00000$, the $0^{*}1^{*}$ monotone
set.  Let $s_{i},s_{j}\in{\cal H}_{1}$ be the two $F_{2}$ homologues.
With a cut $k$ in the second meiosis

$g_{ijk}=s_{i}[1\!:\!k]\,s_{j}[k+1\!:\!5]
     =0^{a}1^{\,b}0^{\,c}1^{\,d},\qquad a+b+c+d=5,\;a,b,c,d\ge0,$

i.e. up to the fixed orientation an $F_{3}$ chromatid is a $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$
word with $a_{10}\le1$.  The $1\to0$ free words are the six monotone
$ s_{i}=0^{i}1^{5-i}$,

$N_{1}=n+1=6.$

Let the unique $1\to0$ descent, if it exists, be at $p$, $1\le p\le4$.
The $p$–prefix can be chosen in $p$ monotone ways ending in $1$ and the
$5-p$ suffix in $5-p$ monotone ways beginning in $0$, so that

$N_{p}=p\,(5-p)$

words have the descent at $p$ and

$N_{10}=\sum_{p=1}^{4}p(5-p)=4+6+6+4=20=\binom{6}{3}$

words have exactly one $1\to0$ descent.  Hence on the arbitrarily chosen
$+$ strand

$N_{+}=N_{1}+N_{10}=6+20=6+\binom{6}{3}=26$

different single–chromosome words can be present in the $F_{3}$ gamete
pool.  The six words $0^{i}1^{5-i}$, $0\le i\le5$, are the $F_{2}$ pool
and the

$0^{a}1^{\,k-a}0^{\,b-k}1^{\,5-b},\qquad0\le a<k<b\le5,$

$20=\binom{6}{3}$ words, e.g. $00101,01001,01101,01011,\dots$, are the
genuinely new $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ $F_{3}$ recombinants.  The
$2^{5}-26=6$ words with two $1\to0$ descents are unattainable with the
fixed left$\to$right asymmetry.

In ordered maternal/paternal notation this is $26^{2}=676$ ordered pairs
and

$\displaystyle\binom{26+1}{2}=351$

unordered diploid autosomal genotypes on the $+$ strand, $20$ of the
$26$ haplotypes being strictly novel in $F_{3}$.  With the usual
internal–only convention $1\le k\le4$ the telomeric $k=0,5$ products are
removed, the $F_{1}\to F_{2}$ pool becomes the four internal monotone
$0^{a}1^{5-a}$, $1\le a\le4$, and the $F_{2}\to F_{3}$ $+$ strand pool is
the four $F_{2}$ types together with the four two–break types
$01011,01001,01101,00101$, i.e. $8$ distinct $+$ strand chromatids,
$8^{2}=64$ ordered and $\binom{8+1}{2}=36$ unordered diploid autosomes,
the $4$ new $F_{3}$ haplotypes normally quoted.  This is the
$6+\binom63$ $a_{10}\le1$ count, $20$ novel $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ haplotypes
on top of the six $F_{2}$ monotone background, often quoted as the
$26\to351$ fixed–orientation $F_{3}$ diversity. ∎

2.text:
On the + strand put $P_{0}=0^{5}$ and $P_{1}=1^{5}$ and with the
asymmetry write a meiosis as the left to right splice 

$$R_{k}(X,Y)=X[1:k]Y[k+1:5]\qquad 0\le k\le5 .$$

$F_{1}\to F_{2}$.  With $P_{0}/P_{1}$ the gamete pool on the + strand is

$${\cal H}_{1}=\{s_{i}=0^{i}1^{5-i},0\le i\le5\},\qquad |{\cal H}_{1}|=6,$$

the six monotone $0^{*}1^{*}$ words.  Let $s_{i},s_{j}\in{\cal H}_{1}$ be
the two $F_{2}$ homologues and let the $F_{2}\to F_{3}$ cut be $k$.  On
the fixed strand

$$R_{ijk}=s_{i}[1:k]s_{j}[k+1:5]
      =0^{\min(i,k)}1^{\,k-\min(i,k)}0^{\max(0,j-k)}1^{\,5-k-\max(0,j-k)} ,
$$

i.e. up to the fixed orientation an $F_{3}$ chromatid is a
$0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ word

$$w=0^{p_{1}}1^{p_{2}}0^{p_{3}}1^{p_{4}},\qquad p_{1}+p_{2}+p_{3}+p_{4}=5,
\;p_{i}\ge0,$$

with $a_{10}\le 1$, at most one $1\to0$ descent.  The $a_{10}=0$ class is
the $F_{2}$ pool

$$N_{1}=5+1=6,\qquad s_{i}=0^{i}1^{5-i},$$

$11111,01111,00111,00011,00001,00000$.  Let the unique $1\to0$
descent be at $p$, $1\le p\le4$.  The $p$–prefix can be chosen in $p$
ways as a monotone word ending in $1$ and the $5-p$ suffix in $5-p$
ways as a monotone word beginning in $0$, i.e.

$$N_{p}=p(5-p) $$

words have the descent at $p$ and

$$N_{10}=\sum_{p=1}^{4}p(5-p)=4+6+6+4=20 $$

$0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ words with exactly one $1\to0$ descent.  Hence
on the arbitrarily chosen + strand

$$N_{+}=N_{1}+N_{10}=6+20=6+\binom63=26$$

different single-chromosome haplotypes can be present in the $F_{3}$
gamete pool.  Six of them are the $F_{2}$ monotone $0^{*}1^{*}$ types
and

$$N_{\rm new}= \binom63 =20$$

of them, $0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{\,b-k}1^{5-b}\;$ with $0\le a<k<b\le5$, e.g.
$01011,01001,01101,00101,\dots$, are the genuinely new $F_{3}$
$0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ recombinants.  The six $2^{5}-26$ words with two
$1\to0$ descents, $01010,10101$, etc., are unattainable with the fixed
orientation.

In ordered diploid notation the $26$ haplotypes give $26^{2}=676$
maternal/paternal pairs and

$$\displaystyle \binom{26+1}{2}=351 $$

unordered diploid autosomal genotypes in $F_{3}$, the six monotone
types being the $F_{2}$ pool.  The $20$ $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ words are
the $ \binom{6}{3}$ strictly novel $F_{3}$ positive-strand haplotypes
usually quoted.

Remark.  With the strict internal-only convention $1\le k\le4$ the two
telomeric products $k=0,5$ are removed.  The $F_{1}\!\to\!F_{2}$ pool is
then the four internal monotone $0^{a}1^{5-a}$, $1\le a\le4$, and the
$F_{2}\!\to\!F_{3}$ + strand pool is the four $F_{2}$ monotone types
together with the four $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ types $01011,01001,01101,
00101$, i.e. eight distinct + strand chromatids, $8^{2}=64$ ordered and
$\binom{8+1}{2}=36$ unordered diploid autosomes, the $4+4$ internal-only
version of the $26\to351$ count above. ∎

On the $+$ strand put $P_{0}=0^{5}$ , $P_{1}=1^{5}$ and with the
asymmetry fixed write a meiosis as the left–right prefix–suffix

$$R_{k}(X,Y)=X[1:k]\,Y[k+1:5],\qquad 0\le k\le 5, $$

on the chosen strand.  The $F_{1}\to F_{2}$ pool is then the monotone

$${\cal H}_{1}=\{s_{i}=0^{i}1^{5-i}:0\le i\le5\},\qquad |{\cal H}_{1}|=6,
$$

$11111,01111,00111,00011,00001,00000$, the six $0^{*}1^{*}$ $F_{2}$
chromatids.

Let $s_{i}=0^{i}1^{5-i}$, $s_{j}=0^{j}1^{5-j}\in{\cal H}_{1}$ be the two
$F_{2}$ homologues and let the $F_{2}\to F_{3}$ cut be $k$.  On the fixed
$+$ strand

$$g_{ijk}=s_{i}[1:k]\,s_{j}[k+1:5]
       =0^{\min(i,k)}1^{\,k-\min(i,k)}0^{\max(0,j-k)}1^{\,5-k-\max(0,j-k)} ,
$$

i.e. up to the fixed orientation

$$g_{ijk}=0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d},\qquad a+b+c+d=5,\;a,b,c,d\ge0, $$

descent.  The $a_{10}=0$ class is the $F_{2}$ monotone set

$$N_{1}=n+1=6,\qquad s_{i}=0^{i}1^{5-i} .$$

Let the unique $1\to0$ descent be at $p$, $1\le p\le4$.  The $p$-prefix
has to be monotone and end in $1$ – $p$ possibilities – and the $5-p$
suffix has to be monotone and begin in $0$ – $5-p$ possibilities – so

$$N_{p}=p(5-p)$$

words have the descent at $p$.  Hence

$$N_{10}=\sum_{p=1}^{4}p(5-p)=4+6+6+4=20
      =\binom{6}{3}$$

words have exactly one $1\to0$ descent, $0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{\,b-k}1^{5-b}$,

recombinants.  With the six $F_{2}$ monotone words

$$N_{F_{3}}^{+}=N_{1}+N_{10}=6+20=26$$

$F_{2}$ monotone $0^{i}1^{5-i}$; the $20=\binom{6}{3}$ words

unattainable with the orientation fixed.

maternal/paternal pairs and

$$\binom{26+1}{2}=351$$

unordered diploid autosomal genotypes in $F_{3}$ on the chosen strand.

3.text:
On the arbitrarily chosen $+$ strand we may write the two completely
inbred founders as

$$P_{0}=0^{5},\qquad P_{1}=1^{5}$$

and with the left $\to$ right asymmetry a meiosis on the chosen strand is
the prefix–suffix splice

$$R_{k}(X,Y)=X[1:k]\,Y[k+1:5],\qquad 0\le k\le5, $$

the obligatory one crossover per gamete.

$F_{1}\to F_{2}$.  With $P_{0}/P_{1}$

$${\cal H}_{1}=\{s_{i}=0^{i}1^{5-i}\;:\;0\le i\le5\},\qquad |{\cal H}_{1}|=6, $$

$11111,01111,00111,00011,00001,00000$,
the $0^{*}1^{*}$ monotone $F_{2}$ gamete pool on the $+$ strand.

Let $s_{i}=0^{i}1^{5-i},s_{j}=0^{j}1^{5-j}\in{\cal H}_{1}$ be the two $F_{2}$
homologues and let the $F_{2}\to F_{3}$ cut be $k$.  On the fixed
orientation

$$g_{ijk}=s_{i}[1:k]s_{j}[k+1:5]=0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d},
\qquad a+b+c+d=5,$$

i.e. an $F_{3}$ chromatid on the $+$ strand is a $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$
word with $a_{10}\le1$, at most one $1\to0$ descent.  The $a_{10}=0$ class
is the $F_{2}$ pool

$$N_{1}=n+1=6,\qquad s_{i}=0^{i}1^{5-i}.$$

Let the unique $1\to0$ descent be at $p$, $1\le p\le4$.  The $p$-prefix
must be a monotone word ending in $1$ – $p$ possibilities – and the
$5-p$ suffix must be a monotone word beginning in $0$ – $5-p$
possibilities. Hence

$$N_{p}=p(5-p)$$

words have the descent at $p$ and

$$N_{10}=\sum_{p=1}^{4}p(5-p)=4+6+6+4=20=\binom{6}{3}$$

words have exactly one $1\to0$ descent.  In the usual parametrisation

$$g_{ijk}=0^{a}1^{\,k-a}0^{\,b-k}1^{\,5-b},\qquad0\le a<k<b\le5,$$

so the $20$ words are the $\binom{6}{3}$ strictly novel $F_{3}$
$0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ recombinants, e.g. $00101,01001,01101,01011,\ldots$.

Hence on the arbitrarily chosen $+$ strand, telomeric $k=0,5$ included,

$$N_{+}=N_{1}+N_{10}=6+20=6+\binom{6}{3}=26 $$

different single-chromosome haplotypes can be present in the $F_{3}$
gamete pool. Six of them are the $F_{2}$ monotone $0^{i}1^{5-i}$ and

$$N_{\rm new}= \binom{6}{3}=20$$

of them are genuinely new $F_{3}$ $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ haplotypes on
top of the $F_{2}$ background.  The $2^{5}-26=6$ words with two
$1\to0$ descents are unattainable with the fixed left$\to$right
asymmetry and two successive one-crossover meioses.

In diploid notation the 26 $+$ strand haplotypes give $26^{2}=676$
ordered maternal/paternal pairs and

$$\binom{26+1}{2}=351$$

unordered diploid autosomal genotypes on the fixed strand, $20$ novel
haplotypes on top of the six $F_{2}$ monotone haplotypes.  This is the
$N(n)=n+1+n(n-1)(n+1)/6$, $N(5)=26$, fixed-orientation count.

Remark.  With the conventional strict internal $1\le k\le4$ convention
the telomeric $k=0,5$ products are discarded.  The $F_{1}\to F_{2}$ pool
is then the four internal monotone $0^{a}1^{5-a},\,1\le a\le4$ and the
$F_{2}\to F_{3}$ $+$ strand pool is the four $F_{2}$ monotone types
together with the four internal two-break types $01011,01001,01101,
00101$, i.e. $8$ distinct $+$ strand chromatids, $8^{2}=64$ ordered and
$\binom{8+1}{2}=36$ unordered diploid autosomes, the usual $4+4$
textbook internal-only version of the $26\to351$ count. ∎

$R_{k}(X,Y)=X[1:k]Y[k+1:5],\qquad 0\le k\le5 ,$

the obligatory one crossover per gamete.  Hence

${\cal H}_{1}= \{s_{i}=0^{i}1^{5-i}:0\le i\le5\}$

is the $F_{1}\to F_{2}$ gamete pool on the $+$ strand,
$|{\cal H}_{1}|=6$, the six $0^{*}1^{*}$ monotone words
$11111,01111,00111,00011,00001,00000$.

Let $s_{i}=0^{i}1^{5-i},\,s_{j}=0^{j}1^{5-j}\in{\cal H}_{1}$ be the two
$F_{2}$ homologues and let the $F_{2}\to F_{3}$ cut be $k$.  On the fixed
strand

$g_{ijk}=s_{i}[1:k]s_{j}[k+1:5]=0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d}$,
$a+b+c+d=5$,

i.e. a $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ word with $a_{10}\le1$, at most one
$1\to0$ descent.  For $i\ge k$ or $j\le k$ the splice collapses to a
monotone $s_{p}$.

$a_{10}=0$ :  $N_{1}=n+1=6$ monotone $s_{i}=0^{i}1^{5-i}$,
the $F_{2}$ pool.

Let the unique $1\to0$ descent be at $p$, $1\le p\le4$.  The $p$-prefix
can be chosen in $p$ monotone ways ending in $1$ and the $5-p$ suffix in
$5-p$ monotone ways beginning in $0$, so

$N_{p}=p(5-p)$

words have the descent at $p$ and

$N_{10}=\sum_{p=1}^{4}p(5-p)=4+6+6+4=20=\binom{6}{3}$

words have exactly one $1\to0$ descent.  They are the
$0\le a<k<b\le5$ splices

$g_{ijk}=0^{a}1^{\,k-a}0^{\,b-k}1^{\,5-b}$,

$20=\binom 63$ genuinely new $F_{3}$ $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ mosaics.

Hence on the arbitrarily chosen $+$ strand

$N_{+}=N_{1}+N_{10}=6+20=6+\binom63=26$

different single chromosome haplotypes can occur in the $F_{3}$ gamete
pool, six of them the $F_{2}$ monotone $0^{*}1^{*}$ types and
$N_{\rm new}= \binom63=20$ strictly novel $F_{3}$ $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$
types.  The $2^{5}-26=6$ words with two $1\to0$ descents, e.g. $01010$,
are unattainable with the fixed left$\to$right asymmetry.

In diploid notation the $26$ $+$ strand haplotypes give $26^{2}=676$
ordered maternal/paternal pairs and

$\displaystyle \binom{26+1}{2}=351$

unordered diploid autosomal genotypes on the fixed strand,
$20$ novel haplotypes on top of the six $F_{2}$ monotone background.

Remark.  With the conventional internal-only convention $1\le k\le4$ the
telomeric $k=0,5$ products are discarded.  The $F_{1}\!\to\!F_{2}$ pool
is then the four internal monotone $0^{a}1^{5-a}$, $1\le a\le4$, and the
$+$ strand $F_{2}\!\to\!F_{3}$ pool is the four $F_{2}$ monotone types
together with the four two-break types $01011,01001,01101,00101$, i.e.
$8$ distinct $+$ strand chromatids, $8^{2}=64$ ordered and
$\binom{8+1}{2}=36$ unordered diploid autosomes, the usual $4+4$
internal-only textbook count. ∎

4.text:
On the fixed orientation put the two inbred founders as $P_{0}=0^{5}$ and
$P_{1}=1^{5}$ and write a one crossover meiosis on the chosen strand as
the left $\to$ right prefix suffix splice

$$R_{k}(X,Y)=X[1:k]Y[k+1:5],\qquad 0\le k\le5 .$$

$F_{1}\to F_{2}$.

With $P_{0}/P_{1}$ the $+$ strand gamete pool is the monotone $0^{*}1^{*}$
set

$${\cal H}_{1}=\{s_{i}=0^{i}1^{5-i}:0\le i\le5\},\qquad |{\cal H}_{1}|=6,$$

$11111,01111,00111,00011,00001,00000$, the six $F_{2}$ haplotypes on the
$+$ strand.

$F_{2}\to F_{3}$.

Let $s_{i}=0^{i}1^{5-i},\,s_{j}=0^{j}1^{5-j}\in{\cal H}_{1}$ be the two
$F_{2}$ homologues and let the second obligatory cut be $k$.  On the
fixed $+$ strand

$$g_{ijk}=s_{i}[1:k]s_{j}[k+1:5]=0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d},\qquad
a+b+c+d=5,$$

i.e. every $F_{3}$ chromatid is a $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ word.  In
particular $a_{10}\le1$, at most one $1\to0$ descent is possible with two
successive one crossover meioses in the fixed orientation.

$a_{10}=0$ : the $F_{2}$ monotone class

$$N_{1}=5+1=6,\qquad s_{i}=0^{i}1^{5-i},$$

$11111,01111,00111,00011,00001,00000$.

$a_{10}=1$. Let the unique $1\to0$ descent be at $p$, $1\le p\le4$. The
$p$–prefix has to be a monotone word ending in $1$ – $p$ possibilities –
and the $5-p$ suffix has to be a monotone word beginning in $0$ –
$5-p$ possibilities. Hence

$$N_{p}=p(5-p)$$

words have the descent at $p$ and

$$N_{10}=\sum_{p=1}^{4}p(5-p)=4+6+6+4=20=\binom{6}{3}$$

$0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ words have exactly one $1\to0$ descent.  In the
normal form

$$g_{ijk}=0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b},\qquad0\le a<k<b\le5, $$

the $20$ words are the $\binom63$ triples $a<k<b$.  They are the
genuinely new $F_{3}$ recombinants, e.g. $00101,01001,01101,01011,\dots$.
The $2^{5}-26=6$ words with two $1\to0$ descents, $01010$ etc., are
unattainable with the orientation fixed.

Hence on the arbitrarily chosen $+$ strand

$$N_{+}=N_{1}+N_{10}=6+20=6+\binom63=26$$

different single chromosome 5-mers can be made by two obligatory
single cross-overs. Six of them are the $F_{2}$ monotone $0^{i}1^{5-i}$
and

$$N_{\rm new}= \binom63 =20$$

of them are strictly novel $F_{3}$ $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ haplotypes with
$b>0,c>0$ on top of the six $F_{2}$ background.  This is the
$6+\binom{6}{3}$ $a_{10}\le1$ count.

In ordered diploid notation the 26 $+$ strand haplotypes give
$26^{2}=676$ ordered maternal/paternal pairs and

$$\binom{26+1}{2}=351$$

unordered diploid autosomal genotypes in $F_{3}$ on the fixed strand,
20 haplotypes being strictly novel in $F_{3}$.  Removing the two
telomeric formal cuts $k=0,5$ the conventional internal-only $1\le k\le4$
version is the four internal $F_{2}$ monotone types together with the
four internal two-break types $01011,01001,01101,00101$, i.e. $8$
distinct $+$ strand chromatids, $8^{2}=64$ ordered and
$\binom{8+1}{2}=36$ unordered diploid autosomes, the $4$ novel internal
$F_{3}$ haplotypes usually quoted. ∎

7.text:
On the strand that is chosen to be $+$ write the two inbred founders as

$P_{0}=0^{5}\qquad P_{1}=1^{5}$

and with the fixed left $\to$ right asymmetry a meiosis on the $+$
strand is the prefix–suffix splice

$$R_{k}(X,Y)=X[1:k]\,Y[k+1:5],\qquad 0\le k\le5 ,$$

an obligatory single crossover in every gamete.  $F_{1}\to F_{2}$

${\cal H}_{1}=\{s_{i}=0^{i}1^{5-i}:0\le i\le5\}$

is the $0^{*}1^{*}$ monotone gamete pool, $|{\cal H}_{1}|=6$,

$11111,01111,00111,00011,00001,00000$,
on the $+$ strand.

Let $s_{i}=0^{i}1^{5-i},s_{j}=0^{j}1^{5-j}\in{\cal H}_{1}$ be the two
$F_{2}$ homologues and let the $F_{2}\to F_{3}$ cut be $k$.  On the fixed
$+$ strand

$$g_{ijk}=s_{i}[1:k]s_{j}[k+1:5]=0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d},
\qquad a+b+c+d=5, $$

i.e. every $F_{3}$ chromatid is a $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ word with at most
one $1\to0$ descent, $a_{10}\le1$.  The $a_{10}=0$ class is the $F_{2}$
pool

$$N_{1}=n+1=6,\qquad s_{i}=0^{i}1^{5-i}.$$

Let the unique $1\to0$ descent, if it is present, be at $p$, $1\le p\le4$.
The $p-$prefix has to be a monotone word ending in $1$ – $p$ possibilities –
and the $5-p$ suffix has to be a monotone word beginning in $0$ – $5-p$
possibilities, so that

$$N_{p}=p(5-p)$$

words have the descent at $p$ and

$$N_{10}= \sum_{p=1}^{4}p(5-p)=4+6+6+4=20=\binom{6}{3}$$

words have exactly one $1\to0$ descent.  In the familiar form

$$g_{ijk}=0^{a}1^{\,k-a}0^{\,b-k}1^{5-b},\qquad0\le a<k<b\le5, $$

the $20$ words are the strictly novel $F_{3}$ $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$
mosaics, e.g. $00101,01001,01101,01011,\dots $ The $2^{5}-26=6$ words
with two $1\to0$ descents, $01010$ etc., are unattainable with two
successive fixed-orientation one cross-overs.

Hence on the arbitrarily chosen $+$ strand

$$N_{+}=N_{1}+N_{10}=6+20=6+\binom{6}{3}=26$$

different 5-mer chromatids can be present in the $F_{3}$ gamete pool,
six of them the $F_{2}$ monotone $0^{*}1^{*}$ types and

$$N_{\rm new}= \binom{6}{3}=20$$

of them genuinely new $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ $F_{3}$ haplotypes on top
of the $F_{2}$ background.  This is $N(n)=n+1+n(n-1)(n+1)/6$, $N(5)=26$,
the $a_{10}\le1$ fixed-orientation count.

In diploid notation the $26$ $+$ strand haplotypes give $26^{2}=676$
ordered maternal/paternal pairs and

$$\displaystyle \binom{26+1}{2}=351 $$

unordered diploid autosomal genotypes on the fixed strand, $20$ novel
haplotypes on top of the six $F_{2}$ monotone haplotypes.  Discarding the
formal telomeric cuts $k=0,5$ the conventional internal-only $1\le k\le4$
count is the four internal $F_{2}$ monotone types together with the four
two-break $F_{3}$ types $01011,01001,01101,00101$, i.e. $8$ distinct
$+$ strand chromatids, $8^{2}=64$ ordered and $\binom{8+1}{2}=36$
unordered diploid autosomes, the usual $4+4$ textbook statement. ∎

5.text:
On the arbitrarily chosen $+$ strand put the founders

$P_{0}=0^{5},\qquad P_{1}=1^{5}$

and write a meiosis with the strand asymmetry as the left to right
prefix–suffix splice

$R_{k}(X,Y)=X[1:k]Y[k+1:5]\qquad 0\le k\le5 $ .

$F_{1}\to F_{2}$ on the fixed strand is the monotone $0^{*}1^{*}$ set

${\cal H}_{1}=\{s_{i}=0^{i}1^{5-i}:0\le i\le5\},\qquad |{\cal H}_{1}|=6,$

$11111,01111,00111,00011,00001,00000$.
Let $s_{i},s_{j}\in{\cal H}_{1}$ be the two $F_{2}$ homologues and let the
$F_{2}\to F_{3}$ cut be $k$.  On the fixed $+$ strand

$g_{ijk}=s_{i}[1:k]s_{j}[k+1:5]=0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d}$,
$a+b+c+d=5$,

i.e. a $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ word with $a_{10}\le 1$, at most one
$1\to0$ descent.  The $a_{10}=0$ class is the $F_{2}$ pool

$N_{1}=n+1=6$.

Let the unique $1\to0$ descent be at $p$, $1\le p\le4$.  The $p$-prefix
can be chosen in $p$ monotone ways ending in $1$ and the $5-p$ suffix in
$5-p$ monotone ways beginning in $0$, so

$N_{p}=p(5-p)$

words have the descent at $p$ and

$N_{10}=\sum_{p=1}^{4}p(5-p)=4+6+6+4=20=\binom{6}{3}$

words have exactly one $1\to0$ descent, the $0\le a<k<b\le5$ splices

$g_{ijk}=0^{a}1^{\,k-a}0^{\,b-k}1^{5-b}$ .

Hence on the arbitrarily chosen $+$ strand

$N_{+}=N_{1}+N_{10}=6+20=6+\binom{6}{3}=26$

different single-chromosome haplotypes can be made by two obligatory
single cross-overs.  Six of them are the $F_{2}$ monotone $0^{i}1^{5-i}$,
$0\le i\le5$, and

$N_{\rm new}=\binom{6}{3}=20$

of them, e.g. $00101,01001,01101,01011\ldots$, are the genuinely new
$0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ $F_{3}$ recombinants.  The $2^{5}-26=6$ words with
two $1\to0$ descents are unattainable with the fixed orientation.

In diploid notation the $26$ $+$ strand haplotypes give $26^{2}=676$
ordered maternal/paternal pairs and

$\displaystyle \binom{26+1}{2}=351$

unordered diploid autosomal genotypes in $F_{3}$ on the fixed strand,
$20$ novel haplotypes on top of the six $F_{2}$ monotone background.

Remark.  With the conventional internal-only $1\le k\le4$ convention the
telomeric $k=0,5$ products are removed.  The $F_{1}\to F_{2}$ internal
pool is the four monotone $0^{a}1^{5-a}$, $1\le a\le4$, and the
$F_{2}\to F_{3}$ $+$ strand pool is those four $F_{2}$ types together with
the four two-break types $01011,01001,01101,00101$, i.e. $8$ distinct
$+$ strand chromatids, $8^{2}=64$ ordered and $\binom{8+1}{2}=36$
unordered diploid autosomes, the usual $4+4$ internal-only textbook
statement.  The $26\to351$ count is the telomeric inclusive fixed
orientation count. ∎

1.text:
On the arbitrarily chosen strand put the two completely homozygous founders as

$P_{0}=0^{5}\qquad P_{1}=1^{5}$

and with the left$\to$ right asymmetry write a meiosis as the prefix–
suffix splice

$R_{k}(X,Y)=X[1:k]Y[k+1:5],\qquad 0\le k\le5 ,$

the obligatory one crossover per gamete.  On the $+$ strand

${\cal H}_{1}=R_{k}(P_{0},P_{1})=\{s_{i}=0^{i}1^{5-i}:0\le i\le5\}$

is the $F_{1}\to F_{2}$ gamete pool.  $|{\cal H}_{1}|=n+1=6$, the six
monotone $0^{*}1^{*}$ words

$11111,01111,00111,00011,00001,00000$,

and every $F_{2}$ individual is $s_{i}/s_{j}$ with $s_{i},s_{j}\in
{\cal H}_{1}$.

Let the $F_{2}\to F_{3}$ cut be $k$ and let $s_{i}=0^{i}1^{5-i}$,
$s_{j}=0^{j}1^{5-j}$ be the two $F_{2}$ homologues.  On the fixed
orientation

$g_{ijk}=s_{i}[1:k]s_{j}[k+1:5]=0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d},\qquad
a+b+c+d=5,$

i.e. an $F_{3}$ chromatid is a $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ word with at most
one $1\to0$ descent, $a_{10}\le1$.  For $i\ge k$ or $j\le k$ the splice
collapses to a monotone $s_{p}$.

$a_{10}=0$ :

$N_{1}=n+1=6$ monotone words $s_{i}=0^{i}1^{5-i}$, the $F_{2}$ pool.

$a_{10}=1$ : let the unique $1\to0$ descent be at $p$, $1\le p\le4$.
The $p$–prefix has to be a monotone word ending in $1$ and can be chosen
in $p$ ways, the $5-p$ suffix has to be a monotone word beginning in
$0$ and can be chosen in $5-p$ ways, so that

$N_{p}=p(5-p)$

words have the descent at $p$ and

$N_{10}=\sum_{p=1}^{4}p(5-p)=4+6+6+4=20=\binom{6}{3}$

distinct $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ words have exactly one $1\to0$ descent.
In the usual form

$g_{ijk}=0^{a}1^{\,k-a}0^{\,b-k}1^{\,5-b},\qquad0\le a<k<b\le5,$

the $20$ words are the $\binom{6}{3}$ triples $a<k<b$, e.g.
$00101,01001,01101,01011,\dots$, the genuinely new $F_{3}$ recombinants.
The $2^{5}-26=6$ words with two $1\to0$ descents, $01010$ etc., are
unattainable with the fixed orientation and two obligatory
single–crossover meioses.

Hence on the arbitrarily chosen $+$ strand

$N_{+}=N_{1}+N_{10}=6+20=6+\binom{6}{3}=26$

different $5$-mer chromatids can be generated by two successive
obligatory single cross-overs.  Six of them are the $F_{2}$ monotone
$0^{i}1^{5-i}$ and

$N_{\rm new}=\binom{6}{3}=20$

of them are strictly novel $F_{3}$ $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ haplotypes on
top of the six $F_{2}$ monotone background.  In general

$N(n)=n+1+\dfrac{n(n-1)(n+1)}{6}=n+1+\sum_{p=1}^{n-1}p(n-p)$,

$N(5)=26$, $N_{10}(5)=20$.

In ordered diploid notation the $26$ $+$ strand haplotypes give
$26^{2}=676$ ordered maternal/paternal pairs and

$\displaystyle\binom{26+1}{2}=351$

unordered diploid autosomal genotypes in $F_{3}$ on the fixed strand,
$20$ novel haplotypes on top of the six $F_{2}$ monotone types.

Remark.  With the textbook internal–only convention $1\le k\le4$ the
telomeric formal cuts $k=0,5$ are discarded.  The $F_{1}\!\to\!F_{2}$
pool is then the four internal monotone types $0^{a}1^{5-a},\,1\le a\le4$
and the $F_{2}\!\to\!F_{3}$ $+$ strand pool is those four together with
the four two–break types $01011,01001,01101,00101$, i.e. $8$ distinct
$+$ strand chromatids, $8^{2}=64$ ordered and $\binom{8+1}{2}=36$
unordered diploid autosomes, the familiar $4+4$ internal–only version of
the $26\to351$ telomeric–inclusive count. ∎

On the strand which is kept fixed put the two inbred founders as

$P_{0}=0^{5}\qquad P_{1}=1^{5}$

and with the one-way asymmetry write a meiosis on the chosen strand as
the left $\to$ right prefix–suffix splice

$R_{k}(X,Y)=X[1:k]Y[k+1:5],\qquad 0\le k\le 5$,

the obligatory one cross-over per gamete.  $F_{1}\to F_{2}$ is then

${\cal H}_{1}=\{s_{i}=0^{i}1^{5-i}:0\le i\le5\},\qquad |{\cal H}_{1}|=6$,

$11111,01111,00111,00011,00001,00000$,

the six monotone $0^{*}1^{*}$ $F_{2}$ chromatids on the $+$ strand.

Let $s_{i},s_{j}\in{\cal H}_{1}$ be the two $F_{2}$ homologues and let the
$F_{2}\to F_{3}$ cut be $k$.  On the fixed $+$ strand

$g_{ijk}=s_{i}[1:k]s_{j}[k+1:5]=0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d},\qquad
a+b+c+d=5,$

i.e. every $F_{3}$ chromatid is a $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ word with
$a_{10}\le 1$, at most one $1\to0$ descent.  The $a_{10}=0$ class is the
$F_{2}$ pool

$N_{1}=5+1=6,\qquad s_{i}=0^{i}1^{5-i}$.

Let the unique $1\to0$ descent be at $p$, $1\le p\le4$.  The $p$-prefix
can be chosen in $p$ monotone ways ending in $1$ and the $5-p$ suffix in
$5-p$ monotone ways beginning in $0$,

$N_{p}=p(5-p)$,

so that

$N_{10}=\sum_{p=1}^{4}p(5-p)=4+6+6+4=20=\binom{6}{3}$

$0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ words have exactly one $1\to0$ descent.  In the
form $0^{a}1^{\,k-a}0^{\,b-k}1^{5-b}$ with $0\le a<k<b\le5$ these are the
$\binom{6}{3}=20$ strictly new $F_{3}$ mosaics on top of the six $F_{2}$
monotone types.  The $2^{5}-26=6$ words with two $1\to0$ descents are
unattainable with the fixed left$\to$right asymmetry and two obligatory
single cross-overs.

Hence on the arbitrarily chosen $+$ strand

$N_{+}=N_{1}+N_{10}=6+20=6+\binom{6}{3}=26$

different single-chromosome haplotypes can be present in the $F_{3}$
gamete pool, $6$ of them the $F_{2}$ $0^{*}1^{*}$ types and $20$ of them
genuinely novel $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ $F_{3}$ types.  In particular the
$20$ novel positive-strand recombinants are the $\binom{6}{3}$ words
$0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{\,b-k}1^{5-b},\;0\le a<k<b\le5$.

In diploid notation the $26$ $+$ strand haplotypes give $26^{2}=676$
ordered maternal/paternal pairs and

$\displaystyle\binom{26+1}{2}=351$

unordered diploid autosomal genotypes on the fixed strand in $F_{3}$,
$20$ novel haplotypes on top of the six $F_{2}$ monotone background.
The $26\to351$ count is the telomere inclusive $k=0,5$ count.  With the
conventional internal-only $1\le k\le4$ convention the telomeric cuts
are discarded, leaving the four internal $F_{2}$ monotone types and the
four internal two-break types $01011,01001,01101,00101$, i.e. $8$
distinct $+$ strand chromatids, $8^{2}=64$ ordered and $\binom{8+1}{2}=36$
unordered diploid autosomes, the usual $4+4$ internal-only textbook
statement. ∎

F1→F2 gametes are the monotone $0^{*}1^{*}$ words $s_i=0^{i}1^{5-i}$, $0\le i\le5$, $|{\cal H}_1|=6$.

An F2 heterozygote $s_i/s_j$ with cut $k$ gives $g_{ijk}=s_i[1:k]s_j[k+1:5]=0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d}$ with $a+b+c+d=5$. Hence every F3 chromatid on the fixed + strand is a $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ word with $a_{10}\le1$, at most one $1\to0$ descent.

$N_{10}= \sum_{p=1}^{4}p(5-p)=4+6+6+4=20=\binom{6}{3}$.

Hence $N_{+}=N_1+N_{10}=6+20=26$ distinct positive-strand haploid chromatids. * telomeric inclusive $k=0,5$ allowed → 26 haploid / 351 unordered diploid, 20 strictly novel recombinant haploids.
* internal-only $1\le k\le4$, $1\le i,j\le4$ removes parental telomeric words → 4 internal F2 monotone + 4 two-break $01011,01001,01101,00101$ = 8 haploid, $8^{2}=64$ ordered, $\binom{8+1}{2}=36$ unordered diploid, the textbook $4+4$ internal version.

$R_{k}(X,Y)=X[1:k]\,Y[k+1:5],\qquad 0\le k\le5$,

the obligatory one crossover per gamete.

${\cal H}_{1}=\{s_{i}=0^{i}1^{5-i}:0\le i\le5\}$,
$|{\cal H}_{1}|=n+1=6$,

$N_{p}=p(5-p)$

and

$N_{10}=\sum_{p=1}^{4}p(5-p)=4+6+6+4=20=\binom{6}{3}$

words have exactly one $1\to0$ descent.  In normal form

$g_{ijk}=0^{a}1^{\,k-a}0^{\,b-k}1^{5-b},\qquad0\le a<k<b\le5,$

the $20$ words are the $\binom63$ strictly novel $F_{3}$

fixed left$\to$right asymmetry and two obligatory single cross-overs.

$N_{+}=N_{1}+N_{10}=6+20=6+\binom{6}{3}=26$

different $5$-mer chromatids can be generated by two successive
obligatory single cross-overs, six of them the $F_{2}$ monotone

$F_{3}$ $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ haplotypes.  In general
$N(n)=n+1+n(n-1)(n+1)/6$, $N(5)=26$.

ordered maternal/paternal pairs and

$\displaystyle \binom{26+1}{2}=351$

unordered diploid autosomal genotypes on the fixed strand in $F_{3}$,

$P_{0}=0^{5}$ , $P_{1}=1^{5}$

$F_{1}\to F_{2}$ :

${\cal H}_{1}=R_{k}(P_{0},P_{1})=\{s_{i}=0^{i}1^{5-i}:0\le i\le5\}$,
$|{\cal H}_{1}|=n+1=6$,

$11111,01111,00111,00011,00001,00000$,

the six monotone $0^{*}1^{*}$ $F_{2}$ chromatids on the $+$ strand.
Every $F_{2}$ individual is $s_{i}/s_{j}$ with $s_{i},s_{j}\in{\cal H}_{1}$.

Put $s_{i}=0^{i}1^{5-i}$, $s_{j}=0^{j}1^{5-j}\in{\cal H}_{1}$ for the two

orientation

$g_{ijk}=s_{i}[1:k]s_{j}[k+1:5]=0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d},\qquad
a+b+c+d=5,$

i.e. an $F_{3}$ chromatid on the $+$ strand is a $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$

$a_{10}=0$ :

$N_{\rm new}=\binom{6}{3}=20$

of them are strictly novel $F_{3}$ $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ haplotypes.

different 5-mer chromatids can be generated by two successive obligatory

$N_{\rm new}=\binom63=20$

of them are genuinely new $F_{3}$ $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ haplotypes on top
of the six $F_{2}$ background.  In general
$N(n)=n+1+n(n-1)(n+1)/6$, $N(5)=26$, $N_{10}(5)=20$.

ordered maternal/paternal pairs and

$\displaystyle\binom{26+1}{2}=351$

unordered diploid autosomal genotypes on the fixed strand in $F_{3}$,
